0299: ### 7.5 Before every HV round
0300: 
0301: - Read the whole plan and every document under review end to end; targeted checks are not holistic. When the operator asks for a reconciliation or projection of problems before HV, present every projected problem to the operator and get confirmation before launching the review (added 2026-10-13, from the operator's rulings of 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13).
0302: - Run a structured what-if pass per requirement, not only a consistency check. Ask what observably happens under: crash, restart, or replay at each step; ordering and concurrency; boundary and malformed input; each host or plugin, including unsupported ones; lifecycle (clear, resume, end, terminal states); isolation (cross-workspace, cross-session, cross-agent); legacy and upgrade; operator-visible output. Where the plan does not state the outcome, add a valid AC tagged with the plan's phase or slice and a named test. Adding a valid AC is always a win.
0303: - Chain rules together to find deadlocks: rules that each pass alone but together leave no accepted remedy.
0304: - Diff against known-good anchors and ask "How did it deviate? How do we get back in line?": (1) the operator's verbatim decisions, (2) current working code and baseline-green behavior, (3) classic patterns such as idempotency keys, transactional outbox with at-least-once delivery and idempotent consumers (never claim exactly-once), write-ahead journal before mutation, optimistic concurrency. Justify any departure explicitly or return to the pattern.
0305: - Check that every field set and code list is defined once and identically everywhere, every mapping edge is backed by a TEST statement and vice versa, and handoff and TODO metadata match the plan.
0306: - Edit only between rounds, never while a round is running.
0307: - Propagation audit: after changing any rule, field set, code, or outcome, search every place that states it (requirements, ACs, TRs, TESTs, wire contracts, use cases, the plan's phase or slice tasks, host tables, handoff, TODO) and update each one, or replace the copies with a reference to one canonical statement. In one review round, three of six findings were rules changed in one place and left stale elsewhere. Large edit batches need this audit most.
0308: - Prefer a traceable key over content matching when pairing records (for example queue position or a shared id rather than a text hash); content can differ in representation between producers.
0309: - Search before adding, and lint mechanically: before writing any new rule, grep the whole document for an existing rule on the same subject; a second rule is a contradiction even if each is fine alone (one round added a two-AC TEST rule beside an existing three-AC one). Check cross-reference classes (FR->TR->TEST mappings, which of the plan's phases or slices owns each named case, phase order) with a small script instead of waiting for the reviewer to find them one per round.
0310: - Enforce the checklist, do not just remember it (operator, 2026-10-10, after this guidance was skipped for many unsupervised rounds): make the pre-HV checklist a hard gate in the HV launcher, which refuses a round unless a per-round self-review record shows evidence for each item (holistic review, what-if, propagation audit, phase boundaries, search-before-adding, no new mechanism, mapping lint, the operator scoping directive verbatim in the brief, standing rules in every delegated brief). Guidance that only lives in memory gets skipped under time pressure.
0311: - Phase-boundary audit: every test or AC you add must be allocated to the plan's phase or slice where everything it depends on already exists (server gate, review verbs, marker fields). A behaviour that ships before its dependency needs an explicit activation contract (for example a server-written capability) and an inert mode, including after a rollback. Check the dependency chain and the rollout order for each new case, not just the AC text.

0313: ### 7.6 When findings come back
0314: 
0315: - Ask "What did I miss?", not only "How do I fix this?". Classify each finding (crash window, cross-session addressing, traceability drift, field-set drift, use case vs requirement contradiction, metadata drift, and so on) and sweep the whole artifact for siblings of each class before the next round.
0316: - Verify each finding against source before acting.
0317: - Separate implementer fixes from operator decisions, and batch operator decisions into one question.
0318: - Recurrence signal: when one design area produces new findings in round after round, the problem is structural, usually a missing traceable key or a missing single source of truth. Stop patching. Diff the area against the known-good pattern (for example single writer, one ordered log, idempotency key), return to it, and delete the mechanism the patches added. One design area failed for five rounds until a single minter reading one ordered log replaced the patches.
0319: - Indistinguishable inputs: when two histories produce byte-identical inputs (a redelivery of one event versus a separate event with equal fields), no derived key can separate them. Adding per-invocation state such as a counter or salt breaks idempotence instead. Run the what-if on both histories, then state the honest limit: fail closed under an existing rule, probe how often it happens, and document it. Never promise two invariants the inputs cannot support. Before a fix, check it against every invariant the old value satisfied (purity, retry reuse, the two-process tests), not only the finding it repairs.

0321: ### 7.7 Writing fixes
0322: 
0323: - Fix the deficient requirement. Reconcile with existing requirements first, strengthen an existing AC second, create a new requirement only when the need is genuinely new.
0324: - Do not add design mechanism (protocols, algorithms, crash choreography) to plan text. State the observable, testable outcome; the how belongs to the contract step of the plan's phase or slice.
0325: - Make each fix minimal, then attack it yourself before the next round; fixes are the main source of new findings. Do not churn text that a prior round accepted.
0326: 
0327: ### 7.8 Design principle and coordination
0328: 
0329: - Always have a traceable relationship when coordinating two disparate entities: every record, event, or message carries the root ids of whatever it is a child of or depends on, so it is attributable on its own. A missing parent id is a design failure. Find the commonality first when relating something new to existing knowledge. Where an external format lacks the key, say so and compensate in your own records; never infer it silently.
0330: - Coordinating with another agent: use one append-only channel with read-back verification. Accept counters that expose real defects; fold refinements in only as minimal ACs. Each effort keeps its own required reviewer and gates; keep cross-effort dependencies acyclic and order-independent. A decision relayed by one agent may not satisfy the other agent's approval controls; the operator may need to state it to each agent directly.

0360: ### 8.2 Decisions are conclusions

0332: 
0333: Ph3 migration fixtures cover every classified project domain and its child/link graph, soft-deleted rows, multiple projects, decimal/UTC/binary/Unicode edge cases, promoted session snapshots, audit records, derived-index rebuild and inert operational metadata. FailedVerifyCannotCutover additionally tests death before provider mapping switch and after switch before reopening: recovery opens exactly one verified provider, retains source bytes and never loses Dolt-only writes. 0001: # Three-system federation walkthrough and requirements
0002: 
0003: Author: Codex. Date: 2026-11-10. Proposed behavior for [the new architecture](2026-11-10-federation-dolt-architecture.md), not a report of deployed behavior. H=LAB-OMARCHY, A=PAYTON-LEGION2, B=isolated test peer FED-ATLAS-B. Project Atlas and symbolic commit names C0/A1/B1/H1/M1 are examples, not real records or hashes. The hub has a local working copy and a separate shared committed-history remote.
0004: 
0005: ## Standard workflows
0006: 
0007: ### U01: enroll and start the same project
0008: 
0009: H registers Atlas with immutable ProjectId and an initial approved C0. A and B enroll with distinct immutable node tags, map their own filesystem paths to Atlas, receive authorized subscriptions and clone C0. Each can now read and edit locally. An existing nonempty node database is inventoried/migrated, never overwritten by the clone. Server: enrollment, project identity, initial snapshot, scoped credentials. Plugins: discover/select project and branch; show local/remote heads. Requirements: FR-MCP-176,182,185,187.
0010: 
0011: ### U02: node A edits, then commits
0012: 
0013: A edits a TODO. Its local draft survives restart, but H and B remain at C0 and no sync is triggered. A previews and explicitly commits A1; this wakes synchronization. After validated publication, the hub remote is A1 and H/B receive control requests. Their workers fetch and accept A1 on clean branches; their local reads now include the TODO. Server: explicit commits, publication and control generation. Plugins: diff/commit/status; distinguish local commit from publication. Requirements: FR-MCP-174,175,178,179,183,189.
0014: 
0015: ### U03: work directly on the hub
0016: 
0017: H edits in its local working copy while A and B continue independently. H commits H1 and its normal worker publishes it to the shared remote; A/B receive requests. H's uncommitted draft before H1 neither travels nor prevents A/B publication because the hub remote is a separate repository. Requirements: FR-MCP-174,175,178,184.
0018: 
0019: ### U04: simultaneous clean edits on all three systems
0020: 
0021: Starting at C0, A commits a title edit A1, B commits an unrelated description edit B1, and H commits a separate requirement H1. A publishes first. B fetches A1, Dolt merges A1+B1 into M1, validation passes and M1 publishes. H fetches M1, merges H1 into M2 and publishes. A/B accept M2. Every original commit remains an ancestor. A publication race returns head_changed and repeats fetch/merge; no force push. This assumes nonconflicting cells and valid domain relationships. Requirements: FR-MCP-178,181,188.
0022: 
0023: ### U05: conflicting edits to the same field
0024: 
0025: A and B both change one requirement's priority from the same base to different values and commit independently. A publishes A1. B receives A1 while holding B1; merge reports a conflict. B retains its last valid local state, and H/A retain A1. B's plugin displays base/local/incoming values and requests review. A reviewed resolution creates M1 including both histories, passes validation and publishes; H/A then accept it. Changed heads invalidate an old resolution. Delete/update and schema conflicts use the same visible review boundary. Requirements: FR-MCP-180,181,183.
0026: 
0027: ### U06: hub unreachable, then reconnect
0028: 
0029: The A/B-to-hub link fails; H retains local access to its own gateway and remote. H, A and B still execute local business operations and make H1/A1/B1 commits. H may publish H1 locally while A/B record pending publication; they do not return queued-only results for local business writes. On reconnect A merges H1+A1 into M1 and publishes, then B merges M1+B1 into M2 and publishes; H/A catch up to M2. They authenticate, reconcile remote heads and process requests plus their own unpublished commits. Merge/review follows U04/U05. An empty hub queue does not strand local commits. No automatic hub failover is claimed. Requirements: FR-MCP-174,175,178,179,181,185.
0030: 
0031: ### U07: incoming commit while node B has a draft
0032: 
0033: B has uncommitted edits at C0. A publishes A1; B polls and fetches history, but records waiting_local_work instead of committing, discarding or overwriting its draft. B's user finishes the draft and explicitly commits B1 (or separately chooses another authorized disposition). Then reconciliation proceeds. Fetch succeeded does not mean the branch was synchronized. Requirements: FR-MCP-175,180,183,189.
0034: 
0035: ### U08: divergent feature work and deliberate merge
0036: 
0037: A creates feature/search from C0 and commits F1. Publication shares feature/search; main remains C0 on all systems. B selects feature/search to inspect or continue it and commits F2. H can review the branch data. An authorized explicit merge into main creates M1 and triggers normal publication. Branch selection is per session, never a process-wide switch. No PR is created. Requirements: FR-MCP-177,180,183,189.
0038: 
0039: ### U09: lost response or crash during synchronization
0040: 
0041: A publishes A1 but loses the success response. H has A1 and unsatisfied subscription state. A restarts, checks remote ancestry and its request receipt, and recognizes publication without creating A2 or repeating an external business action. A missed hub state update is repaired by head-generation reconciliation. A new worker epoch rejects stale reports from the old worker. Reporting generation g must not clear desired g+1. Requirements: FR-MCP-179,181,188.
0042: 
0043: ### U10: migrate an existing project
0044: 
0045: Both real lab stores are SQLite. The migration tool additionally supports PostgreSQL and SQL Server fixture sources. It plans those sources, inventories local-only versus shared data, detects legacy-ID collisions and checks the Dolt schema. Ph3 delivers seed and all-domain/all-branch project recovery export (including the TODO subset); Ph6 adds join only after branch/commit/publication/review exist. Exactly one seed establishes C0 per project. Other nodes clone C0 and import their frozen legacy differences on migration branches descended from C0, then merge/review them normally. Verification accounts for source rows already in C0, mapped deltas and explicitly reviewed exclusions/deletions. Include TODO/generic audit history in the independent hub backfill and verify every durable receipt. Detect same-work/different-ID duplicates for review and preserve permanent origin-scoped aliases, without rewriting historical text. A failed verification leaves the original provider active. No unrelated root histories or implicit deletion of seed rows are allowed. Requirements: FR-MCP-182,184,186,187.
0046: 
0047: Same-identity rows with different legacy contents require a recorded keep-seed/take-join/manual-value review before the join commit, even if Dolt would merge cleanly. Verify the immutable migration commit and the reviewed main result; keep destination writes closed until integration and verification finish.
0048: 
0049: ### U11: node running an older schema/application
0050: 
0051: H's maintenance role publishes a supported schema upgrade. B advertises an older capability and records incompatible_schema; it does not apply it or claim to be current. B may continue supported local work while publication is held. After preflight and binary upgrade, B merges S1 with its retained unpublished B1 to form M1, validates and publishes M1, then H/A accept M1. Both B1 and S1 remain ancestors; B does not simply replace B1 with S1. Each feature branch catches up separately through review/validation. Nodes never independently run EF migrations on versioned project startup. Incompatible contract changes wait for subscriber acknowledgement or explicit de-enrollment/recovery. Requirements: FR-MCP-181,183,186.
0052: 
0053: Before swapping B's binary, its owners explicitly commit or resolve all drafts and the schema head must be available locally; otherwise upgrade waits without touching drafts. B attests every local branch, including unpublished ones. Maintenance preflight gates deployment. Each branch reopens only after its local worker merges the designated schema history and validation passes; a catch-up conflict blocks that branch only. The new EF model never edits an unsupported dirty working set or independently executes project migrations.
0054: 
0055: ### U12: two agents on one host
0056: 
0057: Two plugins select Atlas/main on A. Only the editing lease owner may mutate its working set. The other agent reads or selects a separate branch. The first agent's commit preview binds to its expected working-set fingerprint; takeover cannot silently absorb its draft. Plugin reconnect revalidates the lease and context. Requirements: FR-MCP-177,183,189.
0058: 
0059: ### U13: audit reaches the hub without a project commit
0060: 
0061: Precondition: A is enrolled in Atlas; main=C0 and A has authorized local audit storage. A edits T1 while offline, appending immutable audit E1 and its outbox entry. On reconnect, audit/batches sends E1 through the IdentityServer gateway, independent of Dolt commits. The hub stores it append-only and returns a hash-bound receipt. A lost receipt causes retry, not duplication; the node retains E1 permanently. Postcondition: one E1 at each origin/hub ledger, main and remote still C0, local draft preserved. Errors: invalid_token, unauthorized_project, audit_id_conflict. Requirements: FR-MCP-AUDIT-001, FR-MCP-184/185/188. Ph2/Ph3/Ph5/Ph7.
0062: 
0063: ### U14: duplicate work, permanent aliases and human IDs
0064: 
0065: Precondition: frozen LAB TODO-7 and LEGION TODO-91 describe the same task. Planning emits similarity evidence; it does not infer identity automatically. An authorized review chooses keep-both or one canonical entity with both scoped IDs retained as aliases. Historical commits, PRs, session logs, memories and documents remain unchanged. For new human labels, two concurrent reservations of IMPL-UNITGREEN-001 yield one owner and one human_id_reserved response. Offline work uses a tagged provisional ID until reservation succeeds. Postcondition: every old reference remains resolvable with origin context, no unreviewed row disappears, and an ambiguous unqualified ID reports ambiguous_legacy_id. Requirements: FR-MCP-182/187. Ph2/Ph3/Ph5/Ph6.
0066: 
0067: ### U15: restore a hub older than a node
0068: 
0069: Precondition: A1 was published under epoch E1/generation90 and remains on A/B, but the backup contains C0/generation40. Restore keeps ingress disabled, installs a fresh E2 and advertises only verified restored heads. A node's E1 report receives hub_epoch_changed; it retains A1. The hub requests candidate history and validates ancestry before republishing A1 under E2. Audit inventories reconcile independently and permanent node ledgers resend missing records. Postcondition: no force push or forced node rewind, all recovered history preserved, receipts refer to E2 and no missing audit row is falsely acknowledged. Requirements: FR-MCP-179/181/184/188. Ph5/Ph6/Ph8.
0070: 
0071: ## UC preconditions, success and exception coverage
0072: 
0073: U01 starts with authenticated owner/node enrollment and empty target; succeeds with shared C0 and distinct local paths; nonempty/foreign target is denied. U02 starts with editable C0; succeeds with explicit A1 and eventual peer acceptance; draft or failed publication remains local. U03 is U02 on H with a separate shared remote. U04 starts at common C0 and three distinct edits; succeeds at M2 preserving H1/A1/B1/M1; conflict takes U05. U05 starts with same-base conflicting commits; succeeds only at an authorized valid merge; stale preview is rejected. U06 starts with enrolled peers and link loss; succeeds after M1/M2 reconciliation without queued-only local writes. U07 starts with a dirty B branch; succeeds only after the owner explicitly disposes the draft and merge validates; waiting age remains visible. U08 starts with C0 and authorized feature creation; sharing leaves main unchanged and explicit merge creates M1. U09 starts with an accepted commit and lost reply; retry returns the same hash/receipt without replay. U10 starts with retained frozen sources; success requires seed/join accounting, reviewed aliases, audit receipts and verified main; any failed verify blocks cutover. U11 starts with an unsupported incoming schema and unpublished work; success preserves B1 plus S1 ancestry after preflight and M1 validation; dirty/unattested branches block upgrade. U12 starts with agent1's edit lease; agent2 reads or selects another branch; no commit captures agent1's draft. U13-U15 state their own preconditions/postconditions above. Exact row/head/error assertions are canonical TEST-MCP-222..237 criteria, not inferred from diagram labels.

0001: # Federation: existing-solution options for operator decision
0002: 
0003: 2026-11-10. Codex. Research proposal, not a dependency adoption or compatibility certification.
0004: 
0005: ## Decision requested
0006: 
0007: Keep LAB-OMARCHY as hub and PAYTON-LEGION2 as first spoke. Prefer supported library facilities over custom authentication, HTTP forwarding, retry queues and synchronization. Approve or deny the candidates below before dependency adoption. Recommendations are engineering judgments; documented capabilities and remaining unknowns are distinguished below.
0008: 
0009: Operator clarification, 2026-11-10: local nodes perform the same business work as the hub, remain operational when disconnected, and exchange updates with the hub in both directions. Evaluate libraries against that intended behavior. This supersedes the earlier forwarding-first recommendation; it does not establish when the implementation diverged from the operator's original intent.
0010: 
0011: Subsequent operator decisions: branches are in the initial release; concurrent edits use Git-style merging with conflicts reviewed at the receiving node; pull requests are out of scope. The operator then asked for Git with relational storage. The most relevant new options are G (Dolt: versioned relational data), H (Fossil: distributed version control stored in SQLite), and I (literal Git via relational libgit2 object backends). These are distinct architectures, not interchangeable packages. Earlier A-F remain reference candidates; their earlier ranking is superseded by this question. Dotmim.Sync and Wolverine must demonstrate branch/history fit rather than being treated as complete solutions. Operator decision 2026-11-11: Dolt (option G) is selected as the versioned-storage engine; the other options remain reference candidates. No package is adopted or installed by this document, and engine feasibility remains gated by Ph0 B1.
0012: 
0013: ## A. Reuse the existing identity integration: Duende IdentityServer
0014: 
0015: Repository evidence: `Directory.Packages.props` pins Duende.IdentityServer 7.4.7 and its AspNetIdentity/EntityFramework packages at 7.4.6. The existing host integration has client-credentials support and static clients. Its current SQL Server wiring is an application configuration fact, not evidence that Duende supports only SQL Server.
0016: 
0017: Duende documents reference tokens with introspection and operational persistence, plus EF configuration and operational stores. Reuse supported issuer, credential, persistence and revocation facilities rather than inventing another credential or revocation ledger. Application authorization still must bind the authenticated user, node and allowed workspaces. A client-credentials token by itself is not proof that a human signed in.
0018: 
0019: Approval scope: retain Duende and design federation authentication around its supported facilities. Before implementation, verify the installed v7 APIs, runtime/provider compatibility, package alignment and deployment entitlement. Choose token mode and revocation/cache behavior against the approved outage requirements. Current online documentation may describe newer versions; it does not prove those APIs exist in the pinned version.
0020: 
0021: Sources: [reference tokens](https://docs.duendesoftware.com/identityserver/tokens/reference/), [EF stores](https://docs.duendesoftware.com/identityserver/data/providers/entityframework-core/), [v7 client model](https://docs.duendesoftware.com/identityserver/reference/v7/models/client/).
0022: 
0023: ## B. Replace forwarding mechanics: YARP
0024: 
0025: Microsoft's `Yarp.ReverseProxy` supplies `IHttpForwarder`, including streaming, dynamic destination selection and response forwarding. Direct forwarding does not supply retries, application routing or authorization policy. Our code would still decide the authorized hub/workspace, enforce hop limits, and protect internal headers.
0026: 
0027: Recommendation: remove YARP from the critical federation path for the clarified local-processing model. Evaluate it only if an independent proxy requirement remains after reconciliation. It does not provide database synchronization or offline business execution.
0028: 
0029: License: MIT in the upstream repository. Exact package version and dependency compatibility remain to be pinned before adoption.
0030: 
0031: Sources: [Microsoft direct-forwarding documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/servers/yarp/direct-forwarding?view=aspnetcore-10.0), [license](https://github.com/dotnet/yarp/blob/main/LICENSE.txt).
0032: 
0033: ## C. Replace durable delivery machinery: Wolverine
0034: 
0035: Wolverine documents transactional inbox/outbox persistence, EF Core integration and an HTTP messaging transport with retries and durable outbox support. The HTTP transport avoids requiring a separate broker. Its SQLite integration documents file-backed persistence; its durability documentation also covers SQL Server and PostgreSQL.
0036: 
0037: Wolverine supports CQRS-style command handling as well as durable messaging. Recommendation: a candidate for publishing committed domain changes, not a complete replication solution. It can replace delivery/retry infrastructure, but conflict resolution and state convergence still need evidence. This fit is an inference until the exact version/provider/transaction combination is tested. Do not replay a locally executed business command remotely if doing so would repeat external side effects.
0038: 
0039: Wolverine is not a turnkey database synchronizer. Domain enumeration, canonical IDs, ownership and parity checks remain application concerns. Determine whether an existing backfill needs a separate progress marker at all when durable message acceptance owns progress. Never equate inbox deduplication with globally exactly-once effects.
0040: 
0041: Before adoption prove: domain mutation plus outbox write share the intended transaction on every required provider; receiver apply plus inbox state recover after crashes; HTTP endpoints enforce node/workspace authorization; duplicates and lost acknowledgements produce no extra effects; old queue rows can be preserved and migrated without two active delivery owners. If this needs a new custom transport or durability engine, reject that integration design and compare option D.
0042: 
0043: License: MIT in upstream. Exact package versions, support policy and transitive dependencies remain to be pinned.
0044: 
0045: Sources: [durability](https://wolverinefx.io/guide/durability/index.html), [EF Core integration](https://wolverinefx.io/guide/durability/efcore/), [HTTP transport](https://wolverinefx.io/guide/http/transport.html), [SQLite persistence](https://wolverinefx.io/guide/durability/sqlite.html), [license](https://github.com/JasperFx/wolverine/blob/main/LICENSE).
0046: 
0047: ## D. Replace database synchronization machinery: Dotmim.Sync
0048: 
0049: Dotmim.Sync is a .NET database-synchronization framework with web client/server components. Its current source tree includes SQL Server, SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB provider projects. This makes it a serious candidate for initial and incremental hub/spoke synchronization, potentially removing more of F3/F4 than a messaging library.
0050: 
0051: Recommendation: retain as a synchronization candidate, subject now to proof of branch/history/merge fit. Source-tree presence does not establish a released, supported PostgreSQL package or its behavior. Older documentation says PostgreSQL is future work; resolve that discrepancy from a pinned release, package metadata and tests, rather than rejecting or accepting it on stale docs. Its documented default conflict policy is ServerWins; that is a library default, not an approved product decision.
0052: 
0053: Key fit questions: can server-enforced workspace filters prevent foreign-workspace data access; can hub-owned fields remain authoritative; do mixed-provider schemas, FK graphs, tombstones and canonical identifiers match the approved data model; does direct table synchronization preserve required domain validation and audit behavior; can existing data be provisioned without destructive schema work? A need for broad bespoke providers or engine modifications would undermine the speed benefit.
0054: 
0055: License: MIT in upstream. No package installed; release/runtime/provider support remains unverified.
0056: 
0057: Sources: [project](https://github.com/Mimetis/Dotmim.Sync), [provider and web project inventory](https://github.com/Mimetis/Dotmim.Sync/tree/master/Projects), [older overview](https://dotmimsync.readthedocs.io/Overview.html), [license](https://github.com/Mimetis/Dotmim.Sync/blob/master/LICENSE).
0058: 
0059: ## E. External replication engine: SymmetricDS
0060: 
0061: SymmetricDS offers heterogeneous database replication and lists SQL Server, PostgreSQL and SQLite. Its current editions page requires Java 21+, lists Community under AGPLv3 with 15-minute synchronization intervals, and commercial editions with shorter intervals. Verify connector availability and limits for the exact edition before selecting it.
0062: 
0063: This is an option if a separately operated replication service is acceptable. It could reduce in-process replication development, but adds an operational component and does not establish application authorization, ownership or domain validation. Recommendation: retain as an alternative rather than the first choice for this .NET service; exact licensing eligibility, cost, deployment and policy fit are unresolved. No license purchase or service installation is authorized.
0064: 
0065: Sources: [official editions and platform list](https://symmetricds.org/editions/), [official FAQ](https://symmetricds.org/docs/faq/).
0066: 
0067: ## Common acceptance evidence before adoption
0068: 
0069: - Pin a released version, license, maintainer provenance and runtime support. Follow `docs/context/compliance-rules.md`; maintainer origin and deployment license entitlement are not yet certified by this research.
0070: - Enumerate the existing components removed, reused or retained. Migration preserves old queue/checkpoint records and never silently discards unacknowledged operations.
0071: - Demonstrate SQLite, SQL Server and PostgreSQL where required by the approved product scope. Actual lab-provider inventory remains a separate prerequisite.
0072: - Prove ownership isolation, unauthenticated denial, hub-authoritative fields, duplicate delivery, lost acknowledgement, crash/restart and offline recovery using approved contract cases. Prove record/relationship parity independently of the library's own success flag.
0073: - Measure implementation and operational burden after the compatibility evaluation. Do not claim a calendar saving without evidence.
0074: - Prove independent branches, retained common ancestors, three-way merge behavior and review of incoming conflicts. Neither reliable message delivery nor two-way row synchronization alone proves these capabilities. Pull-request infrastructure is out of scope.
0075: 
0076: The operator can approve or deny D, choose C for domain-change replication instead, request E, or reject individual candidates. A remains the existing identity integration; B is no longer a federation prerequisite. Approval of an evaluation does not approve production adoption; the final plan records the exact chosen versions, integration boundaries and migration contract for approval. No default custom engine is authorized when an option fails.
0077: 
0078: Additional primary sources for the clarification: [Wolverine durable messaging](https://wolverinefx.io/guide/durability/), [Dotmim.Sync conflict handling](https://dotmimsync.readthedocs.io/Conflict.html). The latter is versioned 0.9.5 documentation, so verify the selected release rather than treating it as current-package proof.
0079: 
0080: ## F. Evaluate actual Git for versioned workspace state
0081: 
0082: The operator identified Git's distributed model as the intended federation model and approved branches for this release. Evaluate native Git or a maintained binding for actual history/branch/merge operations. Git's three-way content merging is available through [git merge-file](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-file); ancestry selection is a separate responsibility described by [git merge-base](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-base). Reuse these facilities instead of implementing a bespoke merge algorithm.
0083: 
0084: This is a candidate requiring an integration design: define the branchable record representation, local database consistency/recovery, histories, relationship validation and transport authorization. Git alone does not make a successful text merge a valid domain transaction. Native Git 2.56.0 was observed on LAB-OMARCHY; cross-host/runtime and binding/license evaluation remain pending. No claim is made that Git or a .NET binding has already been selected as the storage authority. Pull requests, forge integration and automated PR review are explicitly excluded from the initial release.
0085: 
0086: ## G. Dolt: a relational database with distributed version control
0087: 
0088: Dolt is a MySQL-compatible SQL database with commit, branch, merge, clone, fetch, push and pull operations exposed through its CLI and SQL facilities. Its upstream repository uses Apache-2.0. It is a database engine with Git-like semantics, not Git configured to store objects in an arbitrary existing SQL Server/PostgreSQL database.
0089: 
0090: Recommendation: strongest current functional candidate to evaluate for the clarified branchable relational-data design. It may remove the need to invent history, branch synchronization and merge infrastructure. That is an architectural fit judgment, not verified compatibility with McpServer. It would require an explicit provider/storage migration decision and an EF/schema/transaction evaluation.
0091: 
0092: Material difference requiring operator approval: Dolt merges data cell by cell and records data/schema conflicts. It uses relational primary keys for row identity and has special JSON merge behavior. This is not Git's line-based file merge algorithm. Its conflict facilities may be better suited to relational data, but do not silently substitute them for the operator's requested algorithm. The application's review requirement must prohibit unreviewed destructive conflict resolution. Operator decision 2026-11-11: the operator accepted Dolt's cell-level relational merge, with mandatory conflict review, as satisfying the Git-style merging requirement for this release.
0093: 
0094: Local copies exchange data via configurable remotes; the docs include self-hosted and SSH/HTTPS options. No DoltHub subscription or PR system is proposed for initial release. Doltgres provides a PostgreSQL-compatible alternative in the same ecosystem; compatibility does not mean it is a plugin for stock PostgreSQL. DoltLite is a SQLite-derived engine with its own storage implementation; the vendor calls it Beta. The October 2026 vendor update specifically identifies remotes and concurrency/durability as continuing focus areas. Do not assume Dolt, Doltgres and DoltLite can replicate interchangeably without checking their formats and protocols.
0095: 
0096: Sources: [Dolt repository and license](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt), [merge semantics](https://www.dolthub.com/docs/concepts/dolt/git/merge/), [conflicts](https://www.dolthub.com/docs/concepts/dolt/git/conflicts/), [remotes](https://www.dolthub.com/docs/concepts/dolt/git/remotes/), [product variants](https://www.dolthub.com/), [storage-engine distinctions](https://www.dolthub.com/blog/2026-06-17-what-people-are-saying-lwn/), [DoltLite Beta](https://www.dolthub.com/blog/2026-08-31-doltlite-beta/), [DoltLite October status](https://www.dolthub.com/blog/2026-10-12-doltlite-gets-better/).
0097: 
0098: ## H. Fossil: a distributed repository stored in SQLite
0099: 
0100: Fossil stores its repository state, immutable artifacts and derived metadata in SQLite. It provides local clones, branching, merging, push and pull as an existing distributed version-control system. This directly demonstrates that relational storage can underpin the proposed model.
0101: 
0102: It is a different DVCS with Git import/export facilities, not the Git implementation or Git's exact merge engine. SQLite stores Fossil artifacts; this does not automatically version McpServer's existing business tables or supply an EF mapping. Evaluate supported artifact integration and local database consistency before selecting it. Additional built-in collaboration features do not expand the initial-release scope. License and dependency integration review remain pending.
0103: 
0104: Sources: [Fossil technical overview](https://fossil-scm.org/home/doc/trunk/www/tech_overview.wiki), [Fossil versus Git](https://fossil-scm.org/home/doc/trunk/www/fossil-v-git.wiki).
0105: 
0106: ## I. libgit2 with SQL object-database backends
0107: 
0108: The libgit2 organization's `libgit2-backends` repository contains SQLite and MySQL object-database backends. This is the most literal example found of Git objects in an RDBMS. It is a collection of backend components rather than a complete ready-to-run federation platform.
0109: 
0110: Before considering adoption, verify current libgit2 API compatibility, maintenance, license, reference storage, transaction/recovery behavior and .NET binding support. An object backend alone does not prove all repository state resides in SQL or that a complete secure synchronization service exists. The repository's open PostgreSQL backend proposal is not evidence of a released supported PostgreSQL backend. Do not adopt a custom-backend development project by calling it library reuse.
0111: 
0112: Sources: [backend repository](https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2-backends), [open backend proposals](https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2-backends/pulls).

0001: # Federation correctness evaluation: is Dolt-versioned federation the CORRECT way to proceed?
0002: 
0003: Author: ClaudeCode. Date: 2026-11-11. Status: DRAFT decision-support (built while the plan-readiness HV iterated toward AGREE). This is not a requirement, not a plan, and not an approval. It is the case the operator asked for: after HV establishes a VALID way to proceed, decide whether it is the CORRECT way. The architecture decision is the operator's; this document builds the evidence, criteria, risks and a labeled recommendation so he can make it.
0004: 
0005: Observation vs inference is marked throughout. Receipts (web sources) are listed at the end.
0006: 
0007: ## 1. The two different questions
0008: 
0009: - VALID (what HV answers): is the plan internally consistent, decision-complete, and free of rule violations, so a less-capable implementer could execute it without inventing unstated decisions? The R2->R4 HV loop answers this for the packet.
0010: - CORRECT (this document): is Dolt-versioned-relational federation, with the independent-node + hub + guarded-publication architecture, the right thing to build for the operator's actual problem, versus the alternatives, given its external risks, costs and maturity? HV cannot answer this by being more internally consistent; the decisive facts are external to the packet.
0011: 
0012: ## 2. What "correct" means here (decision criteria)
0013: 
0014: 1. Problem-fit: does the design serve the operator's stated intent (independent nodes; bidirectional sync; Git-style branches IN; merge with mandatory conflict review; two-char node tags; PRs OUT) with low impedance mismatch?
0015: 2. Best-among-alternatives: among the surfaced options (library-options A-I), is Dolt the best fit for THOSE requirements?
0016: 3. Critical-dependency feasibility: can the single load-bearing dependency (a maintained EF Core 10 provider driving Dolt over the MySQL wire on net10.0) be satisfied without violating the operator's dependency rules?
0017: 4. Maturity and operational risk: is the engine production-sound for a small lab that may grow, and what operational burden does it add?
0018: 5. Complexity vs value (V-squared): is the build proportionate to the value, or over-engineered for two hosts plus a logical test peer?
0019: 6. Reversibility and lock-in: if the bet is wrong later, how cleanly can the operator get his data back out?
0020: 7. Sequencing and optionality: can the decision be de-risked by proving the uncertain parts before committing the irreversible ones?
0021: 
0022: ## 3. The case FOR (points that this is correct)
0023: 
0024: - 3.1 Best structural fit for the stated requirements (inference, high confidence). The operator asked for branches, three-way merge with review, and retained history on project DATA. Dolt provides commit/branch/merge/clone/fetch/push/pull natively on relational tables. Among the surfaced options, nothing else gives native relational history+branching: Dotmim.Sync is row synchronization with a ServerWins default and no history/branch model; Fossil is a SQLite-backed DVCS but does not map the existing EF business tables; libgit2 SQL backends are a custom-development project, not library reuse. So for the operator's EXACT requirements, Dolt is the strongest fit the research found. (Receipt: library-options.md options D, F, G, H, I.)
0025: - 3.2 The plan is structured to answer "correct" before committing (observation). Ph0 is a disposable feasibility harness with twelve blocking outputs (B1-B12), all initial status "unproven," and it explicitly forbids silent EF downgrade, a prerelease provider, or a bespoke provider; it requires reporting concrete alternatives if compatibility fails. Nothing in Ph1-Ph8 is authorized until Ph0 is accepted. So the plan already treats the engine/provider bet as a gated spike, not an assumption. (Receipt: 2026-11-10-federation-dolt-bdpv4.md section 5; architecture.md section 8.)
0026: - 3.3 Lock-in is partially mitigated by design (observation). Ph3 delivers a verified all-domain Dolt-to-new-SQLite recovery export (every B2 domain, every branch, dirty working sets), with originals kept read-only and a one-node-first 48-hour soak before the second host. This is a real exit path, not a promise. (Receipt: architecture.md section 9; ac-FullProjectRecoveryPreservesAllDomains.)
0027: - 3.4 Dolt is a real, committed engine (observation, from vendor and third parties). Dolt 1.0 shipped in 2023 with a committed storage format and self-describes as production-ready; it supports multi-writer concurrency via standard SQL transactions with a commit/merge layer on top. (Receipt: DoltHub productionizing/concurrency posts.)
0028: 
0029: ## 4. The case AGAINST (risks that this may not be correct NOW)
0030: 
0031: - 4.1 The load-bearing dependency does not yet exist in an acceptable form (observation + inference; HIGH materiality). The repository targets net10.0 and EF Core 10.0.0. As of Oct/Nov 2026:
0032:   - Pomelo.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql, the provider DoltHub itself uses, has NO GA EF Core 10 release. Its latest 9.0.0 constrains EF Core to the 9.0.x range; mixing any EF Core 10 package yields NU1107/NU1608. The EF10 port (PR 2031) is open and unmerged; the tracking issue has been open with a "soon" since Oct 2025. (Receipt: startdebugging.net NU1608/NU1107 post; Pomelo GitHub.)
0033:   - The ONLY confirmed EF Core 10 build is the third-party Microting fork (10.0.7, built on MySqlConnector >= 2.5.0, assembly renamed from Pomelo). A renamed community fork is exactly the "maintained provider / maintainer provenance / deployment entitlement" risk the operator's dependency rules (compliance-rules.md; MEMORY-BESTPRACTICE-001 section 7, NuGet warnings may never be ignored) are strict about. (Receipt: Microting.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql 10.0.x on NuGet.)
0034:   - Oracle's official MySQL Connector/NET EF provider: DoltHub reported "issues" using it, and its EF10 status is unconfirmed here.
0035:   - Inference: at today's state the plan's own B1 gate is likely to FAIL on the "maintained EF10-compatible provider" criterion, forcing one of: (a) accept the Microting fork under explicit risk acceptance; (b) pin the Dolt project context to EF Core 9 while the rest of the solution stays EF Core 10, and absorb the solution-wide version tension; (c) wait for Pomelo EF10 (timeline unknown); or (d) reconsider the engine or the timing. This is the single most decision-relevant fact for "correct NOW."
0036: - 4.2 Engine operational maturity adds burden (observation; MEDIUM). Dolt garbage collection is offline (stop sql-server, run dolt gc); historically it could not reject connections (admins set very high max-connections, improvement status unconfirmed); durability hardening is in progress (crash-recovery testing began Jan 2026 after a VM crash, no published guarantee yet); and the troubleshooting guide warns heavy read concurrency can consume all host CPU. For a two-host lab these are manageable but real, and they land on the operator to run. (Receipt: DoltHub troubleshooting, crash-recovery-testing, server-connections posts.)
0037: - 4.3 Scope/complexity vs value for two hosts (inference; MEDIUM). The design is enterprise-grade: a fourth database provider with its own migration assembly, a full migration tool (plan/run/resume/verify/cutover/abort) across three source providers, a guarded HTTPS publication gateway, IdentityServer reference-token integration with per-node clients, conflict-review storage with ageing, append-only hub audit backfill, all-domain recovery export, and a staged soak cutover. Much of this is intrinsic to doing distributed project data SAFELY, and is to the plan's credit. But the fourth-provider + full-migration-tool slice is a large, mostly-irreversible lift whose value should be weighed against a narrower first increment. The deployment target is two machines (LAB-OMARCHY, PAYTON-LEGION2) plus a logical test peer.
0038: - 4.4 Semantic gap in "Git-style merging" (observation; LOW, already accepted). The operator's mental model is Git. Dolt merges data cell-by-cell with relational conflict detection, not Git line-level text merge. The operator accepted this (U2, 2026-11-11), and the plan is honest about it; recorded here only so the acceptance is explicit in the correctness case.
0039: 
0040: ## 5. Alternatives re-weighed against the STATED requirements
0041: 
0042: - Dolt (option G): best native fit for branches + relational merge + history; cost is the EF10 provider gap and engine operational maturity. 
0043: - Dotmim.Sync (D): mature .NET sync, but row-synchronization with a ServerWins default and no native branch/history/merge-review model; would require building the branch/merge/review layer the operator wants on top. Worse fit for the stated requirements.
0044: - Fossil (H): SQLite-backed DVCS proving relational storage can underpin DVCS, but it versions Fossil artifacts, not the existing EF business tables; would need a custom mapping layer. Worse fit.
0045: - libgit2 SQL backends (I): most literal "Git objects in SQL," but a backend-component collection, not a federation platform; adopting it is a custom-development project. Worse fit.
0046: - Status quo DirectProxy / forwarding: does not meet the core requirement (independent local execution + bidirectional history exchange); explicitly superseded for versioned projects.
0047: - Inference: among options for the operator's EXACT requirements, Dolt is the best fit IF and ONLY IF the EF10 integration can be made sound within the dependency rules. The correctness decision therefore reduces largely to the B1 provider question plus a proportionality judgment on scope.
0048: 
0049: ## 6. The decisive uncertainty
0050: 
0051: Inference (high confidence): "Is this correct NOW?" turns primarily on B1 - whether a maintained, rules-compliant EF Core 10 provider path to Dolt exists. Everything else (fit, lock-in mitigation, plan safety) points toward Dolt being a reasonable choice; the provider gap is what could make "now" the wrong time or the fork the wrong dependency.
0052: 
0053: ## 7. Recommended decision framework (my inference; the decision is the operator's)
0054: 
0055: 1. Make Ph0/B1 a hard go/no-go SPIKE on the provider question specifically, run FIRST and in isolation, before any Ph1-Ph8 commitment. Define its acceptance explicitly: a provider path that (a) supports EF Core 10 on net10.0, (b) satisfies the operator's maintainer-provenance/entitlement and NuGet-warning rules, and (c) passes the real Dolt schema/query/transaction/migration tests the plan already enumerates.
0056: 2. Pre-agree the fallbacks and their acceptance owners, so B1 is a decision point, not a dead end: (a) accept the Microting fork under an explicit, recorded risk acceptance; (b) pin the Dolt project context to EF Core 9 with the solution-version tension evaluated and accepted; (c) defer federation until Pomelo EF10 ships; (d) re-scope or re-select. Each is the operator's call; B1 should present them with evidence, not pick one silently (which the plan already requires).
0057: 3. Consider a reduced first increment to de-risk scope: one project, the two real hosts, a single versioned domain (for example TODOs) end-to-end through commit/publish/merge/review/recovery, BEFORE building the full fourth-provider + full-migration-tool surface. This proves the architecture against reality cheaply and keeps the irreversible lifts optional until the model is validated.
0058: 4. Define the "correct" exit test up front: what Ph0 evidence confirms Dolt-now is correct (a clean provider path + passing real-DB contracts), and what flips it (no rules-compliant provider path, or engine operational blockers on LEGION Windows hosting).
0059: 
0060: ## 8. What would change this recommendation (kill criteria)
0061: 
0062: - If B1 shows no EF Core 10 provider path that satisfies the operator's dependency rules, and the operator will not accept the fork or an EF9-pin, then Dolt-NOW is not correct: wait for provider maturity or re-select. 
0063: - If native Windows Dolt hosting on LEGION (B1/B9) cannot be made a supervised, crash-safe service, the two-host premise weakens and the deployment approach must change before proceeding.
0064: - If, on reflection, the operator's real near-term need is narrower than full versioned federation, the proportionate first step is the reduced increment in 7.3, not the full Ph1-Ph8 build.
0065: 
0066: ## 9. Bottom line (labeled inference, operator decides)
0067: 
0068: Dolt is, on the evidence, the best-fitting engine for the operator's stated federation requirements, and the plan is structured safely enough to find out before committing. The honest caveat is timing and dependency: as of Nov 2026 there is no mainstream, rules-compliant EF Core 10 provider for the MySQL wire, only a community fork, and Dolt's operational hardening is in progress. So the correct way to proceed is not "approve Ph1-Ph8 now" and not "abandon Dolt," but "run Ph0/B1 as an isolated, fallback-instrumented provider-and-hosting spike, with a reduced first increment in view, and let B1's evidence make the engine-and-timing call." That keeps the valid plan and makes the correctness decision on evidence rather than optimism.

0083: ## 11. Operator decision update (2026-11-11): accept the unfinished EF Core 10 driver
0084: 
0085: Operator decision (verbatim intent): "I am not afraid of using the unfinished efcore 10 driver and submitting patches for it if necessary."
0086: 
0087: Effect on this evaluation:
0088: 
0089: - Resolves the decisive uncertainty of section 6 in favor of proceeding. The provider risk in 4.1 is no longer a blocker: the accepted path is to use the in-progress EF Core 10 provider (the Pomelo EF10 port PR, or the Microting fork) and contribute upstream patches as needed. The "wait for a maintained GA provider" option is explicitly declined.
0090: - It is a conscious override of the maintained-provider / prerelease-provider dependency posture. Per the operator's authority to relax a rule for a workspace, a prerelease or community-fork provider, patched by this project, is now an accepted dependency for the Dolt project context. The plan's B1 and architecture section 8 wording that forbids a prerelease or bespoke provider must be amended to record this exception (a between-rounds plan edit, deferred until the running HV round completes).
0091: - B1 is reframed, not removed. Acceptance is no longer "a maintained EF10 provider exists" but "the chosen EF10 provider (port or fork), patched as needed, drives Dolt correctly on net10.0 and passes the real schema/query/transaction/migration contracts." Willingness to patch makes B1 a tractable engineering spike the operator owns; it is not yet proof that it works.
0092: 
0093: Two honest residuals the decision does NOT eliminate:
0094: 
0095: - Two separate surfaces. Patching the EF Core 10 PROVIDER fixes the .NET integration layer (C#, patchable by the operator). Dolt's own "not 100 percent MySQL compatible" gaps (query features, SQL translation edge cases) live in Dolt's Go engine; they are worked around or patched UPSTREAM in Dolt, not in the provider. Ph0 must probe both surfaces; the provider decision only de-risks the first.
0096: - Engine operational maturity and scope. Section 4.2 (offline GC, durability hardening, read-concurrency CPU, Windows hosting) and the scope-proportionality judgment (4.3) stand unchanged. The reduced single-project/single-domain first increment (7.3) remains the recommended de-risk and is now the main lever, since the provider blocker is removed.
0097: 
0098: Updated bottom line: with the provider risk operator-accepted, Dolt-NOW is a defensible correct path. Proceed with Ph0/B1 reframed as a provider-ENABLEMENT spike (make the EF10 port/fork drive Dolt, patching as needed, and prove it against the real contracts), keep a reduced first increment in view, and treat Windows hosting (B1/B9) and Dolt-side SQL gaps as the remaining go/no-go evidence. The residual kill paths are narrow: an EF10-provider-plus-Dolt combination that no reasonable patching can make pass the required semantics, or LEGION Windows hosting that cannot be made crash-safe.

---
name: "pdf"
description: "Read, create, inspect, render, and verify PDF files where visual layout matters, including fillable AcroForms. Use Poppler rendering plus Python tools such as reportlab, pdfplumber, and pypdf for generation and extraction."
---

# PDF Skill

## When To Use

- Read or review PDF content where layout and visuals matter.
- Create PDFs programmatically with reliable formatting.
- Fill and validate interactive PDF forms.
- Validate final rendering before delivery.

## Tools + Contract Requirements

Immediately before the first create/edit authoring command, run `mark_artifact_operation_started.mjs` successfully exactly once using the command below. Do not run it for read-only work. For edits, replace `create` with `edit`; adjust the expected count and output format to match the requested outputs.



```bash
node container_tools/mark_artifact_operation_started.mjs --operation-kind create --expected-output-count 1 --output-format pdf
```

## Workflow

1. Prefer visual review: render PDF pages to PNGs and inspect them.
   - Use `pdftoppm` from the bundled runtime or system Poppler when available.
   - If unavailable, install Poppler or ask the user to review the output locally.
2. Use `reportlab` to generate PDFs when creating new documents.
3. Use `pdfplumber` or `pypdf` for text extraction and quick checks; do not rely on text extraction for layout fidelity.
4. After each meaningful update, re-render pages and verify alignment, spacing, and legibility.

## Fill And Validate AcroForms

Visual review alone is not a correctness check for a fillable PDF. A page `/Widget` annotation can render a value from its appearance stream while the canonical `/AcroForm/Fields` tree is missing or contains a stale value.

1. Keep the result interactive by default; set `flatten=True` only when the user explicitly requests a completed, static form. Preserve the source PDF, and do not flatten a signed PDF without an explicit workflow decision.
2. Inspect both representations before filling: enumerate fields from `reader.get_fields()` and `/Widget` annotations from every page's `/Annots`, following `/Parent` and `/Kids`. If a widget and a canonical field have the same name but are distinct objects with no `/Parent` relationship, do not call `reattach_fields()` blindly: it can create a second top-level field with the same name. Report the ambiguity or produce a static result.
3. Recover genuinely orphaned widgets, fill all pages, and write the result with `pypdf`:

```python
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
from pypdf.generic import NameObject

reader = PdfReader(input_pdf)
writer = PdfWriter()
writer.clone_document_from_reader(reader)

# Restores widgets that are missing from /AcroForm/Fields.
writer.reattach_fields()
fields = writer.get_fields() or {}
missing = set(expected_values) - set(fields)
if missing:
    raise ValueError(f"Form fields not found after repair: {sorted(missing)}")

values_to_write = dict(expected_values)
if flatten:
    # Paint every existing value before removing every widget.
    values_to_write = {
        name: field.get("/V", "/Off" if field.get("/FT") == "/Btn" else "")
        for name, field in fields.items()
    }
    values_to_write.update(expected_values)

writer.update_page_form_field_values(
    None, values_to_write, auto_regenerate=False, flatten=flatten
)

if flatten:
    # pypdf's flatten=True paints appearances but does not remove widgets.
    writer.remove_annotations(subtypes="/Widget")
    writer.root_object.pop(NameObject("/AcroForm"), None)

with open(output_pdf, "wb") as stream:
    writer.write(stream)
```

4. Reopen the written PDF before delivery. For an interactive result, require every expected field to be present in `get_fields()` with the expected `/V`, enumerate page widgets again, and confirm their effective `/V` (the widget value or inherited `/Parent` value) agrees. Confirm each updated widget has a non-empty `/AP` `/N` appearance and render the final pages to catch stale or clipped appearances. Do not rely on `/NeedAppearances` or a successful PNG render as proof that logical field data was updated.
5. For a flattened result, require zero `/Widget` annotations and no remaining `/AcroForm` field tree after reopening, then render the final pages. Keep an editable copy when the user may need to revise the form.

## Temp And Output Conventions

- Use `tmp/pdfs/` for intermediate files; delete them when done.
- Write final artifacts under `output/pdf/` when working in this repo.
- Keep filenames stable and descriptive.

## Dependencies

Prefer the Codex bundled workspace/runtime dependencies when available. The primary runtime is expected to include:

- Python packages: `reportlab`, `pdfplumber`, `pypdf`
- Rendering tools: `pdftoppm` and `pdfinfo` from Poppler

If a dependency is missing, install only what is needed.

Python packages:

```bash
uv pip install reportlab pdfplumber pypdf
```

If `uv` is unavailable:

```bash
python3 -m pip install reportlab pdfplumber pypdf
```

System tools for rendering:

```bash
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install poppler

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install -y poppler-utils
```

If installation is not possible in this environment, tell the user which dependency is missing and how to install it locally.

## Environment

No required environment variables.

## Rendering Command

```bash
pdftoppm -png "$INPUT_PDF" "$OUTPUT_PREFIX"
```

## Quality Expectations

- Maintain polished visual design: consistent typography, spacing, margins, and section hierarchy.
- Avoid rendering issues: clipped text, overlapping elements, broken tables, black squares, or unreadable glyphs.
- Charts, tables, and images must be sharp, aligned, and clearly labeled.
- Use ASCII hyphens only. Avoid U+2011 and other Unicode dashes.
- Citations and references must be human-readable; never leave tool tokens or placeholder strings.

## Final Checks

- Do not deliver until the latest PNG inspection shows zero visual or formatting defects.
- Confirm headers, footers, page numbering, and section transitions look polished.
- Keep intermediate files organized or remove them after final approval.

## Final response

### Final Response Citations

- **Create/edit:** for created or edited PDFs, cite each final deliverable exactly once with `purpose="output"`, in its own paragraph. Briefly describe the result without repeating its filename, path, or link. Never put output directives inside prose or list items.
- **Q&A and summaries:** Every file whose contents you summarize or use to support an answer MUST receive a `:codex-file-citation{...}` with `purpose="source"` in the final response. Use the source citation in place of the filename, wherever the filename would appear. Do not write the filename separately and append its citation at the end. Files merely inspected but not used in the answer need no citation. Do not emit output citations for unchanged files or read-only answers.

- Emit `:codex-file-citation{...}` directly, without backticks, code fences, or a Markdown-link wrapper. Use verified targets only. No need to cite or reference intermediate work.

For file citations, set `path` to the verified absolute file path on the task host. Omit `mode`.

Some illustrative examples, real responses use verified targets outside code fences.

```text
:codex-file-citation{path="/absolute/path/review.pdf" purpose="output"}
```

```text
The review of :codex-file-citation{path="/absolute/path/review.pdf" purpose="source"} is due Friday.
```


### Additional Citation Guidance

For PDF Q&A, inspect complete relevant pages and preserve material headings, table/figure labels, footnotes, sources, and sample sizes. PDF citations support only plain file citations; do not add `artifact_kind`, `page_number`, or other locators.

Intended for local-only overrides not committed to source control.\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060Program.cs\\u0060, \\u0060NetEscapades.Configuration.Yaml\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-CFG-005\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022System-Wide Default Copilot Model Propagation\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022Setting the default Copilot model for all session types requires updates to three locations:\\n- \\u0060CopilotClientOptions.Model\\u0060 default value (in \\u0060McpServer.Common.Copilot\\u0060) - controls server-initiated CLI invocations via \\u0060ICopilotClient\\u0060.
