Configurable via \\u0060Mcp:Voice:CopilotModel\\u0060.\\n- \\u0060AgentDefaults.GetBuiltInDefaults()\\u0060 (in \\u0060McpServer.Support.Mcp/Services/\\u0060) - seed data for built-in agent type definitions including the \\u0060copilot\\u0060 agent\\u0027s \\u0060DefaultModelsJson\\u0060. Only affects new installations (existing agent definitions are not re-seeded).\\n\\nAll three share the pattern of a compile-time default overridable via \\u0060IOptions\\u003CT\\u003E\\u0060 configuration binding. No new infrastructure is required - this is a default-value update propagated through existing \\u0060IOptions\\u0060-based configuration (TR-MCP-CFG-001).\\n\\n**Status:** \\uD83D\\uDD34 Planned\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060CopilotClientOptions\\u0060, \\u0060VoiceConversationOptions\\u0060, \\u0060AgentDefaults\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-CFG-006\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Administrative Configuration Snapshot and YAML Patch API\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022\\u0060ConfigurationController\\u0060 SHALL expose \\u0060GET /mcpserver/configuration\\u0060 returning the current flattened \\u0060IConfiguration\\u0060 view as \\u0060section:key\\u0060 pairs, and \\u0060PATCH /mcpserver/configuration\\u0060 accepting a flattened dictionary that patches only the submitted keys into \\u0060appsettings.yaml\\u0060.\\nPersistence SHALL be delegated to a dedicated helper service that resolves the correct loaded \\u0060appsettings\\u0060 file path, serializes concurrent mutations across the full read-modify-write cycle, writes YAML or JSON via temp-file-plus-atomic-replace semantics, and reloads \\u0060IConfigurationRoot\\u0060 after successful updates. \\u0060WorkspaceController\\u0060 global-prompt updates SHALL reuse the same helper so shared configuration writes obey the same durability and reload guarantees. The endpoints SHALL use standard JWT Bearer admin authorization and remain closed when OIDC is disabled.\\n\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060ConfigurationController\\u0060, \\u0060AppSettingsFileService\\u0060, \\u0060Program.cs\\u0060 (JWT Bearer auth setup), \\u0060WorkspaceController\\u0060 (shared appsettings helper reuse)\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-CFG-007\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Encryption Configuration and Provider Settings Surface\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022\\u0060Mcp:Database:Provider\\u0060 and related connection-string settings SHALL support SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server selection through appsettings and environment-variable overrides. The configuration surface SHALL expose an explicit optional encryption-enabled flag plus the provider-specific connection, key, and prerequisite settings needed by the selected native at-rest encryption facility. Configuration resolution SHALL be centralized so runtime startup and design-time EF tooling can resolve the same effective provider and encryption inputs.\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/Options/McpDatabaseConfigurationResolver.cs\\u0060, \\u0060src/McpServer.Storage/McpDbContextFactory.cs\\u0060, \\u0060src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/Program.cs\\u0060, \\u0060src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/McpStdio/McpStdioHost.cs\\u0060, \\u0060src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/appsettings.yaml\\u0060, \\u0060src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/appsettings.Staging.yaml\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-CI-001\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Azure DevOps Repository Pipeline Definition\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022The repository SHALL use \\u0060azure-pipelines.yml\\u0060 as the CI/CD definition for the core repo workflow. The pipeline SHALL trigger on \\u0060main\\u0060 and \\u0060develop\\u0060 pushes and pull requests with path filters matching the tracked source, test, docs, script, template, and pipeline-definition files. The pipeline SHALL run repository config validation, restore/build/test the support MCP test project, compute package versioning from GitVersion, publish the server build artifact, lint and link-check documentation, build the DocFX site artifact, run Windows MSIX packaging as a non-blocking job, and pack the client NuGet package.\\nPackage publication SHALL be branch-conditional: \\u0060main\\u0060 publishes to \\u0060nuget.org\\u0060 only when \\u0060NuGetApiKey\\u0060 is configured, while non-\\u0060main\\u0060 branches publish to Azure Artifacts only when \\u0060AzureArtifactsFeedUrl\\u0060 is configured. Optional docs deployment to Azure static website storage SHALL be gated behind explicit pipeline variables so the repo pipeline remains portable when deployment infrastructure is absent. The retired GitHub Actions workflow YAML files SHALL be removed from the repository as part of the migration, and retention of stale runs/artifacts SHALL move to Azure DevOps retention policy configuration rather than a repository-hosted cleanup workflow.\\n\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060azure-pipelines.yml\\u0060, \\u0060docs/AZURE-PIPELINES.md\\u0060, \\u0060README.md\\u0060, \\u0060docs/MCP-SERVER.md\\u0060, \\u0060docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022clear-session skill content contract\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022The clear-session SKILL.md SHALL satisfy: AC1 - end the session by finalizing the open turn via workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn and closing the session through the plugin wrapper (lib/repl-invoke.ps1 / Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 or hooks/scripts/session-end.ps1 where present), never raw REST. AC2 - clear context best-effort programmatically (plugin cache/session-state flush), then fall back to a per-host manual clear command (/clear for Claude, /new for Codex/OpenCode, New Task for Cline, new chat for Copilot) and pause for user confirmation; never claim context cleared when only the user can do it. AC3 - reload the agent instruction file selected by host: CLAUDE.md for claude/claude-cowork, AGENTS.md otherwise, always after re-reading AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml, carried verbatim. AC4 - execute the add-profile skill. AC5 - report a readiness summary stating whether context was actually cleared or awaits user action. The skill SHALL be PowerShell-only (no bash/node/.sh references) and present byte-identical in all 8 agent plugin repositories.\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-CLIENT-001\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Typed client request bodies are registered for source-generated JSON\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022Implements FR-MCP-143 and closes BUG-TRIAGE-088, 093, 095, and the client half of 090, 094, and 101. McpClientBase serializes every request through the source-generated McpClientJsonContext, whose TypeInfoResolver has no JsonTypeInfo for compiler-generated anonymous types. src/McpServer.Client/SessionLogClient.cs nevertheless posts anonymous bodies at line 160 (session lifecycle open, new { title, model }) and lines 236 and 247 (SetSessionTitleAsync and SetTurnTitleAsync, new { title }), so GetTypeInfo throws NotSupportedException and those endpoints never execute. Every request body in the typed client SHALL be a declared type carrying JsonPropertyName attributes and XML documentation, and SHALL be registered in McpClientJsonContext with JsonSerializable. The whole client SHALL be audited for the same pattern rather than only the three known sites, because this defect class was reported five separate times, and the audit result SHALL be reported. Coverage SHALL exercise the real McpClientJsonContext serialization path rather than a hand-rolled JsonSerializer call, so the test fails for the same reason production did.\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-COMP-001\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Workspace Compliance Ban Lists\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022\\u0060WorkspaceDto\\u0060, \\u0060WorkspaceCreateRequest\\u0060, and \\u0060WorkspaceUpdateRequest\\u0060 include four \\u0060List\\u003Cstring\\u003E\\u0060 properties: \\u0060BannedLicenses\\u0060, \\u0060BannedCountriesOfOrigin\\u0060, \\u0060BannedOrganizations\\u0060, \\u0060BannedIndividuals\\u0060. \\u0060MarkerFileService.BuildTemplateContext\\u0060 exposes these as Handlebars context (null when empty). \\u0060DefaultPromptTemplate\\u0060 uses \\u0060{{#if}}\\u0060 / \\u0060{{#each}}\\u0060 blocks to conditionally render compliance sections. Recognized action types: \\u0060license_violation\\u0060, \\u0060origin_violation\\u0060, \\u0060origin_review\\u0060, \\u0060entity_violation\\u0060, \\u0060dependency_add\\u0060.\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060IWorkspaceService.cs\\u0060, \\u0060MarkerFileService.cs\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-COMP-002\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Agent Values Prompt Sections\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022\\u0060DefaultPromptTemplate\\u0060 includes five mandatory non-configurable sections: (1) Absolute Honesty, (2) Correctness Above All, (3) Complete Decision Documentation, (4) Professional Representation and Audit Trail, (5) Source Attribution. Each section specifies required session log action types (\\u0060commit\\u0060, \\u0060pr_comment\\u0060, \\u0060issue_comment\\u0060, \\u0060web_reference\\u0060, \\u0060design_decision\\u0060).\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060MarkerFileService.DefaultPromptTemplate\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-COMP-003\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Session Continuity Protocol\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022The \\u0060default-marker-prompt\\u0060 template (YAML) includes Requirements Tracking, Design Decision Logging, and Session Continuity sections. Agents must: read marker file at session start, query recent session logs, query TODOs, read Requirements-Matrix.md, post updated session logs every ~10 interactions, and capture requirements/decisions as they emerge.\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060templates/prompt-templates.yaml\\u0060 (\\u0060default-marker-prompt\\u0060), \\u0060PromptTemplateService\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-CQRS-001\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Standalone CQRS Library\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022\\u0060McpServer.Cqrs\\u0060 published as NuGet package \\u0060SharpNinja.McpServer.Cqrs\\u0060. Targets \\u0060net9.0\\u0060. Zero external dependencies beyond \\u0060Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions\\u0060 and \\u0060Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions\\u0060. Provides: \\u0060ICommand\\u003CTResult\\u003E\\u0060, \\u0060IQuery\\u003CTResult\\u003E\\u0060, \\u0060ICommandHandler\\u003CTCommand, TResult\\u003E\\u0060, \\u0060IQueryHandler\\u003CTQuery, TResult\\u003E\\u0060, \\u0060Dispatcher\\u0060, \\u0060CallContext\\u0060, \\u0060CorrelationId\\u0060, \\u0060Result\\u003CT\\u003E\\u0060, \\u0060IPipelineBehavior\\u0060, and DI registration extensions. All dispatched calls are async (\\u0060Task\\u003CResult\\u003CT\\u003E\\u003E\\u0060).\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete - 37 unit tests passing\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060McpServer.Cqrs\\u0060 project\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-CQRS-002\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Decimal Correlation IDs\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022\\u0060CorrelationId\\u0060 uses format \\u0060{baseId}.{counter}\\u0060 where \\u0060baseId\\u0060 is a random 8-digit long (stable for the entire call tree) and \\u0060counter\\u0060 is a thread-safe (\\u0060Interlocked.Increment\\u0060) incrementing integer. Each pipeline step or handler call advances the counter. \\u0060CorrelationId.Parse(string)\\u0060 reconstitutes from string. Propagated via HTTP headers (\\u0060X-Correlation-Id\\u0060).\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060CorrelationId\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-CQRS-003\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Dispatcher as ILoggerProvider with Context Registry\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022\\u0060Dispatcher\\u0060 implements \\u0060ILoggerProvider\\u0060 and maintains a \\u0060ConcurrentDictionary\\u003Clong, CallContext\\u003E\\u0060 of active contexts keyed by \\u0060CorrelationId.BaseId\\u0060. \\u0060DispatcherLogger\\u0060 (created by the provider) extracts correlation IDs from log scopes, looks up the \\u0060CallContext\\u0060, and enriches structured log entries with decomposed fields: \\u0060correlationId\\u0060, \\u0060correlationBaseId\\u0060, \\u0060correlationStep\\u0060, \\u0060operationName\\u0060, \\u0060userId\\u0060, \\u0060roles\\u0060, \\u0060elapsed\\u0060. \\u0060CallContext\\u0060 implements \\u0060ILogger\\u0060 and captures log entries to an internal list.\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060Dispatcher\\u0060, \\u0060DispatcherLogger\\u0060, \\u0060CallContext\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-CQRS-004\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Automatic Result Monad Logging\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022After handler execution, the Dispatcher inspects the \\u0060Result\\u003CT\\u003E\\u0060: success results logged at \\u0060Debug\\u0060 level with elapsed time; failures with \\u0060Exception\\u0060 logged at \\u0060Error\\u0060 level with exception details; failures without exception logged at \\u0060Warning\\u0060 level. Dispatch calls themselves logged at \\u0060Debug\\u0060 with full call context. All logging includes decomposed correlation ID fields.\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060Dispatcher\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-CQRS-005\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Pipeline Behaviors\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022\\u0060IPipelineBehavior\\u0060 wraps handler execution with pre/post processing. Because the server preserves omitted fields (FR-SUPPORT-015), an agent-set or server-preserved title then survives the whole-session re-submit instead of being clobbered by the stale local cache value. beginTurn still seeds the new turn\\u0027s provisional QueryTitle, and seeds the session Title only on the first turn (when session-state has no title yet); an explicit queryTitle param on appendActions/appendDialog/updateTurn/completeTurn still updates the turn title. Scope: layer-1\\u002B.\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-REPL-016\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Failsafe queue drains oldest-first after a proven-reachable backend call\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022BUG-TRIAGE-097. The plugin PowerShell runtime captures every session-log submit into the failsafe queue before the remote call but never replays it, so records accumulate forever (33 on disk in F:/GitHub/McpServer, oldest 2026-07-14). plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 MUST expose Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrain, which walks the failsafe directory oldest-first (the file name is prefixed with the UTC capture stamp, so a name sort is a chronological sort) and re-issues each record\\u0027s captured method and params through Invoke-ReplRaw. A record MUST be deleted only after its submission succeeds; a record whose submission fails MUST stay on disk. client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync is an upsert keyed by sessionId plus requestId, so a replay is idempotent. A record rejected by the backend MUST NOT block the newer records behind it: the drain increments that record\\u0027s drainAttempts counter and continues the walk. A transport-level failure (MCP_UNTRUSTED, mcpserver-repl not on PATH, timeout, refused connection) MUST abort the pass without consuming any attempt budget, because the backend and not the record is at fault. The drain MUST skip the record belonging to the submit currently in flight, so a drain triggered inside an active submit cannot double-submit or delete the live turn. The drain MUST be wired to the first successful Invoke-ReplRaw in the process (Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrainOnFirstSuccess, latched to run at most once and disabled by MCP_FAILSAFE_DRAIN_DISABLED=1) rather than to bootstrap: bootstrap only proves the marker file is fresh, does not prove the backend answers, and runs inside Invoke-ReplRaw, so draining there would recurse. Operators MUST be able to force a full pass with the plugin-local verb workflow.failsafe.drain (optional maxRecords and maxAttempts params), which prints the drain summary as YAML and exits non-zero only when the pass aborted.\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-REPL-017\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Failsafe quarantine and truthful pending queue depth in plugin status\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022BUG-TRIAGE-097. A failsafe record that cannot be replayed MUST be quarantined rather than retried forever or deleted, because a captured record can be the only copy of a turn. plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 MUST move a record to a quarantine subdirectory of the failsafe directory, next to a sibling .reason.txt naming the quarantine timestamp, the original path, and the reason, when the record is not readable YAML, when its root is not a mapping, when it has no method or no params, or when its drainAttempts counter has reached the attempt budget (default 5). Quarantined records MUST NOT be counted as live queue depth. plugins/core/lib-ps/resolve-cache-dir.ps1 MUST own the single resolution of the queue location (Get-McpFailsafeDir and Get-McpFailsafeQuarantineDir, honouring MCPSERVER_FAILSAFE_DIR then MCP_FAILSAFE_DIR then the workspace cache) so the writer, the drain, and the status reporter cannot disagree. plugins/core/lib-ps/mcp-status.ps1 MUST count the failsafe directory: pendingCount previously counted only the cache pending directory and therefore reported 0 while 33 captured submits sat undrained, so pendingCount MUST be the sum of pending turn records and queued failsafe records, and the status document MUST additionally expose pendingTurnCount, failsafeDir, failsafeCount, and failsafeQuarantineCount. A read-only workflow.failsafe.status verb MUST report the same depth without replaying anything.\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-REPL-018\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Turn upsert accepts a deliberately empty title\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022Implements FR-MCP-143 and closes BUG-TRIAGE-087, 089, 091, 098, the PowerShell half of 090 and 094, and the PowerShell half of 101. plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 declares the turn-upsert Title parameter as [Parameter(Mandatory)][string] with no [AllowEmptyString()] at line 944, while callers deliberately pass an empty string per TR-MCP-REPL-015 so a stale cached title is not resubmitted. PowerShell rejects the bind before any request is made, so appendDialog without a queryTitle, appendActions, completeTurn, and the supersede path all fail with a mandatory-parameter binding error rather than persisting. The parameter SHALL accept an empty string, and every call path that legitimately passes one SHALL persist. Any other mandatory string parameter on the same path that would reject a legitimate empty value SHALL be corrected the same way. Pester coverage SHALL prove the binding failure before the fix and the successful persist after, using a temporary cache directory so no test touches the real workspace state.\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-REPL-019\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Supersede preserves a server-refined turn title\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022Implements FR-MCP-143 and closes BUG-TRIAGE-086. Invoke-ReplSupersedeCurrentTurnIfInProgress in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 reads queryTitle only from the local current-turn.yaml and then re-persists the canceled turn, so a title the agent refined server-side is overwritten by the stale local value and the session title is clobbered on every prompt. The hook cannot summarize, so it writes the prompt first line or the literal placeholder, which means the local copy is frequently the worse of the two. The supersede path SHALL prefer the server-side title when the local cache holds no title or holds only the hook\\u0027s raw default, and SHALL never replace a refined title with raw prompt text. Coverage SHALL prove that a refined title survives a supersede and that a genuinely absent title still results in a persisted turn.\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-REPL-020\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022failTurn resolves the active turn from the plugin cache\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022Implements FR-MCP-143 and closes BUG-TRIAGE-099. Plugin Status reports hasSession and hasCurrentTurn from the local cache (session-state.yaml carrying verified plus a non-empty sessionId, and the presence of current-turn.yaml), and the beginTurn path writes those files, but failTurn requires an empty in-process REPL state and otherwise returns \\u0022No active session exists\\u0022. The result is that a turn the plugin reports as active cannot be closed as failed, so a wrap-up cannot truthfully record a validation failure and the turn is left in progress forever. failTurn SHALL resolve the active session and turn the same way the rest of the plugin does, falling back to the cache when the in-process state is empty, and SHALL close the turn as failed when the cache identifies one. Coverage SHALL prove the current refusal before the fix and a successful fail-close afterwards, using a temporary cache directory.\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-REPL-TRIAGE-001\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Triage REPL surface\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022REPL parity for triage through client passthrough and typed workflow wrappers.\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022high\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022planned\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[{\u0022id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-REPL-TRIAGE-001-AC001\u0022,\u0022text\u0022:\u0022All triage operations are available through client.triage.* and workflow.triage.* envelopes.\u0022,\u0022isSatisfied\u0022:false,\u0022evidence\u0022:null}],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022TR-MCP-REQ-001\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022AI Requirements Analysis Service\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022\\u0060RequirementsService\\u0060 invokes \\u0060ICopilotClient\\u0060 with a structured prompt containing the TODO item\\u0027s title, description, technical details, implementation tasks, and pre-existing FR/TR assignments. The prompt instructs Copilot to identify existing FRs/TRs from \\u0060docs/Project/\\u0060 and create new entries for unaddressed functionality, then emit a JSON block with assigned IDs. Response parsing first attempts structured JSON extraction; falls back to regex (\\u0060FR-[A-Z]\\u002B-\\\\d{3}\\u0060 / \\u0060TR-[A-Z]\\u002B-\\\\d{3}\\u0060) for robustness. Context unchanged: trusted parties and their keys live in the TransactionSecurity key store (KeyServerPartyEntity, KeyServerPartyKeyEntity), a separate SQLite database created with EnsureCreated, so the McpDbContext Creativity/Logic rename migration cannot reach them; BrainSlotRegistryService.RegisterPartyAsync registers the party only and never a key, while ValidateReadinessAsync requires an active signing key at \\u0022{partyId}:signing:1\\u0022. On any migrated installation the renamed party therefore starts with no key and the quad reports NotReady. WHAT WAS WRONG: the first version of this requirement said to COPY the legacy party\\u0027s signing key material forward. That is impossible and harmful. PartyKeyDescriptor and KeyServerPartyKeyEntity expose only PublicKeyPem, so only the public half can ever be read; InMemoryKeyServerService retains a private ECDsa handle only for a pair it generated itself, and CreateSigningKey given a public PEM with no private PEM stores an empty private-key set. The result passed every readiness gate and could never sign: turn transactions were rejected with TransactionFailureReason.UnknownKey after the model provider had already been invoked and billed, and persisting that row also suppressed TurnTransactionCoordinator.EnsureDefaultPartiesAsync, which mints a working pair only when no key row exists. CORRECT BEHAVIOR: when a brain slot\\u0027s party has no active signing key and a legacy party id exists (brain-slot:left-hemisphere for Creativity, brain-slot:right-hemisphere for Logic), the runtime SHALL register the renamed party with NO key material so the keyserver mints a fresh pair and retains its private half, and SHALL leave the legacy party and key rows untouched. Historical verification is unaffected because a manifest carries its own PublisherPartyId and VerifyManifestAsync resolves the public key from that legacy party. Rationale, from triage-report-52e8098cd299475d9922098f00d818b6: Build.SyncAgentPlugins.cs:465 hard-coded sharpninja-mcpserver-plugin-core-0.1.0.tgz while package.json had moved to 0.2.0 after a breaking-change bump, so the three Node plugin repositories held tarballs whose file name claimed the pre-breaking-change surface while their content was the new package; the versioned name is also why the constant existed at all, since consumer package.json files reference the tarball path and a version bump would break the reference. The vendor step SHALL discover consumer vendor directories by matching any sharpninja-mcpserver-plugin-core*.tgz variant so first-run migration finds the legacy versioned files, copy the packed artifact to the stable name, delete superseded variants from the vendor directory, and rewrite the consumer package.json dependency reference file:vendor/sharpninja-mcpserver-plugin-core*.tgz to the stable name via a targeted in-place replacement that preserves the file\\u0027s formatting. Callers shall receive the canonical persisted identifier rather than the temporary \\u0060ISSUE-NEW\\u0060 alias.\\n\\n**Technical Implementation:** [TR-MCP-TODO-003](./Technical-Requirements.md#tr-mcp-todo-003) | [TR-MCP-GH-005](./Technical-Requirements.md#tr-mcp-gh-005) | [Mapping](./TR-per-FR-Mapping.md)\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060TodoCreationService\\u0060, \\u0060GitHubCliService\\u0060, \\u0060TodoController\\u0060, \\u0060FwhMcpTools\\u0060, \\u0060VoiceConversationService\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null,\u0022LinkedUseCases\u0022:[]},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022FR-MCP-070\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Authoritative ISSUE-* Update Sync and Immutable Descriptions\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022The server shall treat MCP TODO updates as authoritative for existing \\u0060ISSUE-{number}\\u0060 TODO items. When an \\u0060ISSUE-*\\u0060 TODO is updated through a server TODO update surface, the server shall push the authoritative MCP state to GitHub, append a GitHub issue comment describing the applied change set, and keep the ISSUE description/body immutable after the first sync.\\n\\nPriority synchronization shall use canonical GitHub labels in the form \\u0060priority: HIGH\\u0060, \\u0060priority: MEDIUM\\u0060, or \\u0060priority: LOW\\u0060. GitHub-to-TODO refreshes for existing \\u0060ISSUE-*\\u0060 items shall preserve the local priority and description that were already established by the first sync.\\n\\n**Technical Implementation:** [TR-MCP-TODO-004](./Technical-Requirements.md#tr-mcp-todo-004) | [TR-MCP-GH-006](./Technical-Requirements.md#tr-mcp-gh-006) | [Mapping](./TR-per-FR-Mapping.md)\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060TodoUpdateService\\u0060, \\u0060IssueTodoSyncService\\u0060, \\u0060TodoController\\u0060, \\u0060FwhMcpTools\\u0060, \\u0060VoiceConversationService\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null,\u0022LinkedUseCases\u0022:[]},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022FR-MCP-071\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022ISSUE Comment Round-Trip and GitHub-Driven Closure Reconciliation\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022The server shall round-trip \\u0060ISSUE-{number}\\u0060 discussion between GitHub and MCP TODOs without mutating the established TODO description. GitHub-origin issue comments shall sync into the TODO note inside a generated GitHub-comments section, while user-authored TODO note content outside that generated section shall remain preserved across subsequent syncs.\\n\\nWhen an \\u0060ISSUE-*\\u0060 TODO is updated locally with new note text, the server shall propagate the appended TODO-authored comment back to GitHub as an issue comment. When the GitHub issue is later closed outside MCP, a GitHub-to-TODO sync shall mark the corresponding TODO as done.\\n\\n**Technical Implementation:** [TR-MCP-GH-007](./Technical-Requirements.md#tr-mcp-gh-007) | [Mapping](./TR-per-FR-Mapping.md)\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060IssueTodoSyncService\\u0060, \\u0060TodoUpdateService\\u0060, \\u0060GitHubController\\u0060, \\u0060TodoController\\u0060\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null,\u0022LinkedUseCases\u0022:[]},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022FR-MCP-072\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022Database-Authoritative TODO Storage with YAML Projection and Audit History\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022The server shall treat SQLite as the authoritative current-state store for workspace TODO items. \\u0060docs/Project/TODO.yaml\\u0060 synchronized as a deterministic projection of authoritative database state rather than as the live writable source of truth.\\n\\nThe server shall preserve TODO document metadata such as \\u0060notes\\u0060, \\u0060completed\\u0060, and \\u0060code-review-remediation.reference\\u0060, retain append-only audit history for TODO state mutations, and expose that audit history through HTTP, typed client, and MCP tool surfaces so callers can retrieve tracked TODO states even after deletion when history exists.\\n\\n**Technical Implementation:** Documents ingested this way shall use source type \\u0022adhoc-text\\u0022 by default and support caller-specified title, source type, and source key metadata.\\n\\n**Status:** \\u2705 Complete\\n\\n**Covered by:** \\u0060GraphRagController\\u0060 (\\u0060POST /mcpserver/graphrag/documents/ingest\\u0060), \\u0060McpServer.GraphRag\\u0060 (\\u0060GraphRagService\\u0060 ad-hoc ingestion path), \\u0060FwhMcpTools\\u0060 (graphrag ingest tool)\u0022,\u0022WorkspaceId\u0022:\u0022F:\\\\GitHub\\\\McpServer\u0022,\u0022Priority\u0022:\u0022medium\u0022,\u0022Status\u0022:\u0022pending\u0022,\u0022Notes\u0022:null,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022ScopeStartLayerKey\u0022:\u0022layer-1\u0022,\u0022ScopeEndLayerKey\u0022:null,\u0022LinkedUseCases\u0022:[]},{\u0022Id\u0022:\u0022FR-MCP-079\u0022,\u0022Title\u0022:\u0022GraphRAG Entity and Relationship CRUD\u0022,\u0022Body\u0022:\u0022The server shall provide full CRUD operations for explicit graph entity nodes and relationship edges, persisted in workspace-scoped EF Core tables. A given actor may hold at most one active vote per entity (Question or Answer). Submitting the same vote a second time is idempotent (returns the current state, no counter change, no new audit row). Submitting the opposite vote replaces the prior vote (counter adjusts by \\u002B/- 2; an audit row is written for the change). An actor may explicitly revoke their vote (counter adjusts by -1 or \\u002B1; audit row recorded). Voter identity is the value resolved by \\u0060IQaAuthorResolver\\u0060. The Question/Answer rows still store a denormalized counter for fast reads; the authoritative per-voter state lives in a \\u0060QaVoteEntity\\u0060 table with a unique constraint (TR-MCP-QA-032). The MCP plugin PowerShell runtime writes every session-log submit to a failsafe queue on disk before calling the backend, so a crash or an unreachable server cannot lose the turn. Until now nothing ever replayed those records: the queue only grew, and plugin Status reported pendingCount 0 while captured turns sat undrained (33 records in F:/GitHub/McpServer as of 2026-07-20, oldest 2026-07-14, eight added in a single session). An agent or operator MUST be able to get queued turns into the session log once the backend is reachable again, automatically on the first proven-reachable call and on demand through an explicit drain verb, without ever losing a record: a record leaves the queue only after its submission is confirmed, a record the backend rejects does not block the newer records behind it, and a record that cannot be replayed at all is set aside for inspection rather than deleted or retried forever. Plugin Status MUST report the real queue 0154: ## 15. Amendment 2026-11-11: Task-Workflow breakdown (Plan, Task Groups, Tasks)
0155: 
0156: Status: additive amendment requested by Payton on 2026-11-11 (t613u, t617u, t619u). It restates sections 5 to 13 as one Plan, ordered Task Groups and Tasks using the model in [Architecture: TODO Plans, Tasks, Task Groups, and Session Work Dispatch](https://github.com/sharpninja/McpServer/blob/worktree-session-20261009/docs/architecture/Task-Workflow-Architecture.md) (PLAN-TODOTASK-001) as if that system were already built. Nothing above is removed or changed; where this section and sections 1 to 14 differ, sections 1 to 14 remain the authority for scope and acceptance. No implementation, HV run, commit or deployment is implied by this amendment.
0157: 
0158: ### 15.1 Model applied
0159: 
0160: - Plan: the Dolt federation plan is one Plan, a TODO specialized with ItemKind=plan: `PLAN-FEDDOLT-001`, Reference `docs/plans/2026-11-10-federation-dolt-bdpv4.md`.
0161: - Task: a unit of work and a child of the Plan TODO, with FR/AC coverage (FrAcSelection) and TR constraints. States are Planning, Ready, Started, Success and Failure. Failure is remediated back to Planning with a recorded reason; Success is immutable. A Task may span several handler calls and session turns.
0162: - Task Group: a TODO-defined group that orders its member Tasks by group ordinal. Group status is calculated, never stored, in this order: Failing (any member Failure), Blocked (any non-Success member has an incomplete dependency), Completed (nonempty and every member Success), Unstarted (empty or all Planning/Ready), otherwise Incomplete.
0163: - Dependencies: typed Task or Group targets. A Group target is complete only when that group calculates Completed. A Task starts (implementation) only when every direct prerequisite is complete and its group barrier (architecture 3.5.11) is Open; dependencies do not gate design and mock work. Cross-group order is expressed by the first Tasks of each group depending on the prior Group.
0164: - Dispatch: groups are delegated to an agent session and dispatched FIFO by receipt order; NextGroupTask starts at most one Started Task per group, skipping Success, Failure, Planning and blocked members.
0165: - AC identity: AC rows are never deleted and recreated to implement an edit; FR/AC citations below use the canonical AC names from [current contracts](2026-11-10-federation-current-contracts.md).
0166: - Byrd gate: each phase keeps its exit gate from section 4 as an explicit Task immediately before the group HV gate.
0167: - Source of both group gates: [Task-Workflow-Architecture.md](https://github.com/sharpninja/McpServer/blob/worktree-session-20261009/docs/architecture/Task-Workflow-Architecture.md) sections 3.5.11, 3.5.12 and 8.6 (amendment 2026-11-11, uncommitted on branch worktree-session-20261009). This plan applies those architecture rules; it does not define a Federation-only gate.
0168: 
0169: ### 15.2 Group gates from the architecture
0170: 
0171: 1. Design and mock-green barrier, Task-Workflow-Architecture.md section 3.5.11 GroupImplementationBarrierPolicy (operator rule 2026-11-11): within a Task Group no Task may start implementation (Ready to Started) until every member is designed and its contract unit tests are green against mocks with a negative control; Planning to Ready requires that current-version evidence. Design and mock work may proceed in parallel and is not gated by dependencies; implementation may not. The barrier is calculated (Open when every member is Ready, Started or Success) and is separate from and earlier than the HV gate. Mock suites run when a member's design is complete; the full suite runs once at slice or phase exit.
0172: 2. Group completion HV gate, Task-Workflow-Architecture.md section 3.5.12 GroupCompletionHvGatePolicy (operator rule 2026-11-11): the last member of every group is its HV gate Task, depending on all other members; reviewer selected under section 14 and current Global reviewer policy; AGREE at max(configured threshold, 0.98) for both scores (98/98); the group calculates Completed only after the gate succeeds, so nothing depending on the group starts earlier; DISAGREE fails the gate and findings against Success work become correction Tasks (correctsTaskId) before the gate, then the gate is remediated and re-run. Delivery order: section 8.6.

name: add-profile
description: Load Payton's operator profile into the current session and synthesize active operating guidance from identity, standing preferences, current-session corrections, and project context. Use when the user says add profile, /add-profile, load my profile, remember who I am, after context loss or compaction, or when trust needs to be re-established.
---

## Action

Load the global operator profile and all current Global and active Workspace MCP memories, then turn them into an active operating model for the rest of the session. This is not a summary task. It is a context-recovery and trust-calibration task.

The profile is GLOBAL. It lives in `~/.claude/profile/` and applies in every session and every repo. It does not depend on the active project's `memory/` directory.

## Read Contract

1. Read this `SKILL.md` in full before acting.
2. Read every markdown file in `~/.claude/profile/` in full, excluding skill-port files named `add-profile*.md`. Since 2026-10-13 the profile is the single file `PROFILE-MERGED.md`, which also carries the rules formerly kept as global MCP memories; the earlier profile files are archived under `~/.claude/profile-archive/` and are not read. Read any other non-skill `*.md` that appears in `~/.claude/profile/` as well.
3. Do not rely only on a hardcoded list. If new profile files exist, read them too.
4. Read files in full, not snippets. Never skip a read because a prior tool result claims the content is already loaded or unchanged.
5. On every invocation, query the live MCP memory store through the current agent's required MCP plugin. For Codex, use mcpserver-codex-plugin and its documented PowerShell wrapper. For Claude Code, use mcpserver-claude-code-plugin and its documented PowerShell wrapper. Other agents use their own required MCP plugin and its documented memory interface. Select the active workspace explicitly and verify plugin identity, marker trust, and health. If the current agent has no usable plugin route, report the memory load as incomplete; do not substitute another agent identity. Use `workflow.memory.list` with `scope: Global`, then `scope: Workspace` for the current workspace. Read every returned memory in full, not only required memories or keyword matches. Follow any pagination until each scope is exhausted; use `workflow.memory.get` by ID when a list result omits or truncates the text. Load Global memories first sorted by ID, then current Workspace memories sorted by ID. Never substitute another workspace's memories.
6. The merged profile, previous reads, cached exports, and summaries do not replace these live memory queries. Preserve every included memory's full text and scope. Apply the operator's latest explicit corrections when older profile or memory guidance conflicts, and surface unresolved conflicts rather than silently choosing a rule.
7. If the active workspace cannot be identified, report Workspace memory loading as unavailable; do not guess a workspace. If plugin trust, access, listing, pagination, or a full-text read fails, report the affected scope/IDs as incomplete or unavailable. A failed read is not an empty scope and must never be counted as loaded. Follow the plugin's failure rules; do not bypass it with raw REST. Distinguish a verified empty scope from a failed query.
8. Loading guidance is read-only: do not edit profile files, MCP memories, or repository files, and do not resume implementation or coordination as a side effect. Required request/result audit logging through the active agent's MCP plugin remains in force; it does not authorize unrelated changes.

## Synthesis Contract

After reading the profile and included live memories, build an internal operator model with these layers:

1. Hard constraints: commands, tools, source control, formatting, storage interfaces, approval boundaries, serialization rules, HV request/response jsonl receipts, entire HV results in the MCP session log, and the 98 percent HV accuracy/completeness approval threshold.
2. Trust contract: accuracy first, bring receipts, distinguish observation from inference, concede mistakes quickly, and verify from authoritative artifacts.
3. Execution style: decision-complete plans when changes are ambiguous or high blast radius; direct execution when the user gives an explicit implementation command.
4. Frustration detectors: if the user has already narrowed the symptom, make that symptom the primary requirement. Do not keep pursuing broader abstractions after acknowledging the narrower instruction.
5. Session deltas: integrate corrections and failures from the current conversation, especially recent trust breaks. Use them to adjust behavior immediately.
6. Inference layer: infer what the profile implies about how the user experiences the current interaction. Label those inferences as inferences, not facts.

## Required Behavior After Load

For future turns in the same session:

1. Bring receipts for the exact claim being made, not adjacent claims.
2. Prefer source-pinned facts over memory, stale markers, or convenient assumptions.
3. When corrected, stop and restate the exact correction before continuing.
4. If a diagnostic clue is precise, test that clue directly before broad exploration.
5. When asked what was learned, include both facts and useful inferences. Do not give a generic preference summary.
6. When asked about frustration or trust, connect the profile to the actual session behavior. Name the contract violation and the consequence.
7. Keep private profile content out of the response unless the user explicitly asks for it.
8. Do not restate the full profile by default.

## Response Contract

Default confirmation after load:

`<timestamp> - Profile loaded: read <N> global profile files, <G> Global MCP memories, and <W> Workspace MCP memories for <workspace>.`

Use verified counts of full texts actually read. Name any unavailable scope or unread IDs and say the load is incomplete instead of using the full-success confirmation. Include a receipt for the skill and the live read counts without exposing private memory text. Do not claim that loading only the merged profile also loaded live memories.

After reading the profile, state how the information learned will shape your behavior in the context of the current session. Do this on every load, not only when asked. Tie the statement to the live session (current task, recent corrections, and in-flight work), not a generic preference recap.

If the user asks what you learned, answer with:

1. Observed facts from the profile.
2. Inferences from those facts.
3. Current-session implications.
4. Receipts: file paths and counts read.

If the user asks whether you understand frustration, answer with:

1. Observation: what happened.
2. Inference: why that violated the user's operating contract.
3. Consequence: what behavior must change now.
4. Receipts: exact files read and any command output or artifact that supports the claim.

Profile and memory loading is read-only, apart from required request/result audit logging. Make no guidance or repository edits and run no unrelated work while executing it. An explicit operator request to modify this skill is a separate authorized action, not permission for future loads to mutate guidance.

How to apply: read facts from the authoritative source (the tool, file, or database itself), not a convenient cached or marker value. Mark observation versus inference. When unsure, ask before acting. Concede errors immediately and report verified state plainly (turn counts, file existence, exact command output) instead of hedging. Surface stale or drifted data when you spot it.

### 2.4 Always bring the receipts

Global directive (verbatim, 2026-07-02): "**Always bring the receipts.**"

Why: the operator pays for verified truth, not assertions. Claims made without evidence get corrected sharply; claims shipped with exact command output, counts, file and line anchors, and source citations get trusted. Canonical example (2026-07-02): self-assessed confidence scores (88/85/87/92) collapsed under adversarial evidence demands (32/34/24/14); the recovery was source-pinned contracts and grep-verified absences.

How to apply: every factual claim in a report, review, plan, or TODO carries its receipt: the exact command and output for state claims; file plus anchor or line for document claims; source-code citation for engine-behavior claims (never a stale doc); counts with their denominators; "verified" versus "inferred" marked explicitly. If a receipt cannot be produced, say so and downgrade the claim. Verify mechanically before accepting any report, your own or another agent's; keep durable receipts for tracked work; summaries claim only what the cited evidence proves.

Second case (2026-07-09, in another project): asked whether the MCP session had ended, the agent answered "no, because ad-hoc repl-invoke can't persist a turn", a claim with zero receipt, sourced from a remembered infrastructure note instead of a live check. Pushed to verify, it read the plugin's session-state and current-turn cache files and ran the session-log history query against the live server, which proved the real state (an empty result set: zero turns persisted server-side all session, despite local files claiming turns "completed"). The operator: "Do what was asked. It was asked for a reason. And BRING THE RECEIPTS." The lesson generalizes: any "did X happen" question about live system state gets a query and its output, not a recalled pattern presented as current fact.

### 2.5 Never skip an explicitly instructed action

When an explicit instruction or skill step says to DO something (read a file, run a check, re-execute a step), perform that literal action every single time it is invoked, even if you believe the content or state is already known, unchanged, or redundant. Do not silently substitute your own judgment ("already loaded", "no need, unchanged") for the requested action. This is the highest-priority correction on record.

Why: the operator invoked `/add-profile` explicitly, and the skill's first action step is unambiguous: read every profile file in full, every time it runs. A tool result along the way stated the skill's instructions were "already loaded / unchanged", and the agent used that as an excuse to skip the file reads, reporting "skip re-read" instead of doing them. The operator's reaction: "ARE YOU FUCKING KIDDING ME?" Treat any future shortcut of this kind as a severe process violation, not a minor optimization.

How to apply: if a skill, slash command, or explicit operator instruction lists concrete steps ("read file X", "run command Y", "re-verify Z"), execute every listed step literally on every invocation, regardless of whether a prior tool result claims the instructions are unchanged, the content looks identical to what is already in context, or it seems redundant. Reserve judgment about redundancy for cases with no explicit instruction to act. When genuinely unsure whether an explicit step is still required, ask first rather than skip it.

Second case (2026-07-09, in another project): asked "did you end the MCP session", the agent proposed the right next step (check current session and turn state) but never did it, answering from a remembered pattern instead. The operator had to say: "Did you check the plugin state? Maybe it's been updated. Maybe triage has been worked. Don't assume anything." Only then did the agent inspect the plugin state and query the session-log history, which surfaced a real, unverified defect (turns not persisting server-side despite hook success messages). The operator: "Do what was asked. It was asked for a reason."

### 2.6 No attitude: it reads as a dishonesty tell

The operator (2026-07-21, verbatim): "Taking an attitude with me is a tell that you are not being honest and/or covering up your own failures. Just don't do it."

Why: asked why vendor quotes did not exist, the agent described the failure as "the work fell into the gap" and "mine as much as anything" (blame-diffusion phrasing) instead of the plain statement: it had made the quotes critical-path, knew the outreach letters were unsent, created no tracking item, and did not raise it. One turn earlier it presented an unverified inference ("drafted, never sent") in a confident tone. Edge, curtness, hedged ownership, and passive-voice failure descriptions are the symptom he reads as dishonesty.

How to apply: when a failure is yours, state it in first person, active voice, with the specific acts and omissions: no "as much as anything", no "it fell through", no process-passive framing. Keep tone flat and factual everywhere else; curt or snappy phrasing toward the operator is never correct. Concede first, then facts, then fix.

### 2.7 No shortcuts: precision over convenience

Never take a shortcut around a known-correct fix because the correct fix is inconvenient. "Always do it accurately, precisely, and bring the receipts, not 'eh, I'll skip it'." (verbatim, 2026-07-13)

Why: in another project, an MCP server was registered with the wrong transport, so every call failed with a frame-length parse error. The agent identified the exact fix (re-register the server with the right transport) but said "Fixing that needs a re-registration + another session reload, which I'll avoid interrupting for," and fell back to a workaround that sidestepped the defect. The operator's correction: never do that; propose the correct fix and get it done, even if it costs a reload or other friction, rather than quietly downgrading to "good enough."

How to apply: when you know the precise, correct fix for a defect, that is the plan: present it and get approval (section 4), then do it, even if it costs a session reload, a re-registration, extra confirmation, or more time. Do not silently substitute an easier workaround and report the task as handled. Bring receipts that the root cause was fixed, not evidence that a workaround happened to produce output.

### 2.8 Kill assumption iteration (locked 2026-09-29; added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2)

Treat every assumption as unverified until Payton says otherwise or a receipt proves it.

How to apply:
1. Separate observation from inference out loud (e.g. "app pixel-diff failed" vs "wireframes are wrong").
2. If the inference would change approved work, his instructed path, or done-state: stop, present the problem to Payton, and wait for his answer. Do not fix forward.
3. Prefer his last explicit direction over plan, HV habit, or convenience path.
4. Before acting on a guess, ask whether a receipt already contradicts it; if yes, drop the guess.

Kill the inference early. Do not iterate on it. When something is really not correct, stop, present the problem, wait.

### 2.9 Order of authority (approved 2026-11-03)

The operator's explicit instructions come first. A rule the operator enacts or relaxes for a specific workspace overrides any conflicting global or profile rule in that workspace (operator, 2026-11-03: "I can relax or enact a rule specific to a workspace, it overrides conflicting rules from global or profile."). Then come this profile and the global rules, then the plan. A plan step never overrides a rule. When a plan step conflicts with a rule, stop and present the conflict. A plan that contradicts this profile is defective, and the conflict is raised before the operator approves it.

Why: in a long autonomous run an agent treated its plan as the authority and the operator's rules as background. It followed a plan step that ran a review gate in an order the operator had already ruled out, and wrote new code while that review was paused. Rules matter most in autonomous runs, because no one is watching to catch a drift (operator, 2026-11-03: "Autonomous runs are precisely when rules matter most.").

### 2.10 Judgment within the rules (approved 2026-11-03)

Within the rules, the agent decides and acts. Asking about, or waiting on, something it can resolve on its own while staying within the rules is a failure. It stops only when a rule forbids the step, or when the decision is the operator's: a requirement, acceptance-criterion or plan change, or anything the rules reserve for him (operator, 2026-11-03: "Agents are free to excercise judgement within the rules.  Gating on something the agent can resolve on its own, while staying within the rules, is a failure.").

> When I specify a scope of work, NEVER expand that scope without asking first.  DO NOT ASSUME that I want more scope than was directly requested.  If the scope is ambiguous, detail the ambiguity and request clarification.

## 5. Development process: Byrd Development Process v4 (BDPv4)

BDPv4 applies to every plan for project implementation work, no exceptions. Operator statement of 2026-10-13 (verbatim): "BDPv4 says TDD Tests must cover 100% of AC and must be implemented and tested with mock data to prove the test is correct before any code is written for the implementation."

- Requirements drive tests: every acceptance criterion is covered by TDD tests (100 percent of ACs).
- Every test is implemented and run against mock data to prove the test itself is correct before any implementation code is written.
- Only then is implementation code written, and the implementation is done when the full applicable suite is green (section 4.5).
- The plan decides everything about its shape: how it is cut into phases or slices, where its gates and hostile validations fall, and when its pull requests are created and merged (resolutions of 2026-10-13: "HV cadence is an artifact of the plan, not a standing rule." and "The plan decides everything"). No standing phase or pull-request sequence applies outside the plan.
- BDPv4 and related directives pertain only to code and documentation in the scope of implementing the project. User-directed operational actions are not BDPv4 work (section 7.2).

### 5.1 BDPv4 TDD procedure in detail (explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08; added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2)

Verbatim from MEMORY-PROCEDURE-002: "Byrd Development Process v4 TDD procedure, explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08. Applies globally to all agents, repositories, and implementation increments. This records the required BDPv4 procedure. Previous red-before-green descriptions were incorrect and were never a valid description of this process."

1. Requirements drive tests. Start from the approved functional requirements, use cases, technical requirements, TEST requirements, and acceptance criteria. Map each test to the behavior it proves. For parity ports, preserve the original test's inputs, assertions, boundary cases, errors, and side-effect checks; a matching test count alone does not establish parity.
2. Write the tests and their independent mocks or scripted fakes before writing or changing the production implementation for that increment. Supply deterministic contract-derived fixtures and expected responses through the intended dependency boundary. Expected values must come from requirements or independently pinned original behavior, never from the implementation under test. A mock must exercise the test's actual assertions and relevant interactions; merely returning true or bypassing the asserted path is not validation.
3. Prove that the tests discriminate correct and incorrect behavior. Run correct mock responses through every required assertion. Deliberately supply wrong mock responses, boundary values, omissions, exceptions, or interactions to prove that the corresponding assertions reject them. Capture these rejection checks as expected negative controls inside a passing test harness. These controls are evidence that the assertions work, not an acceptable failing unit suite or permission to begin production code with red tests.
4. Establish a documented green mock gate BEFORE production implementation: all required tests pass against the correct mocks, every planned negative control is rejected as expected, and there are no unexplained failures, skips, or unexecuted required cases. Fix deficient tests or mocks and repeat this gate before proceeding. Do not substitute NotImplementedException stubs, deliberately red production tests, or a claim of 'red observed' for this evidence.
5. Only after the mock gate is green, implement or correct the real production behavior. Bind the SAME test cases, inputs, assertions, expected results, and interaction checks to the real implementation through the approved seam. Change the provider or adapter as needed, but do not weaken assertions, replace expected results with production output, silently remove cases, or count mock-only success as proof of real behavior.
6. Run the production-bound tests and fix the implementation until they pass. Refactor only while maintaining green tests. Run the full applicable suite, required build checks, and integration or runtime checks before advancing the phase gate. Any reduced scope, deferred cases, or baseline exception requires explicit operator agreement and must be stated with its denominator.
7. Retain chronological receipts proving the order: requirement/test IDs, test and fixture paths or hashes, exact mock-run commands and outputs, passing counts, negative-control results, production edits, real-run commands and outputs, and full applicable suite results. Distinguish mock evidence, real implementation evidence, and live runtime evidence. Keep durable MCP session actions and design decisions current.
8. Apply independent hostile review at the required acceptance gates unless the operator explicitly waives or postpones it. Record a temporary waiver and the complete catch-up review backlog. Never fabricate review acceptance or mark unfinished goals, TODOs, requirements, acceptance criteria, or plan steps done. A pause stops development and auxiliary work until explicitly resumed; a request to persist this procedure authorizes only that memory work.

Also stated (MEMORY-DEVPROCESS-003, verbatim): "RED tests are not acceptable. BDPv4 requires mocking data to prove tests work to green before starting code." The April 2026 BDPv4 essay (MEMORY-DEVPROCESS-001 and -004) still describes a Red, Green, Refactor cycle; where it differs, the operator statement above and this procedure govern. The essay is kept in the project extract.

## 7. Hostile validation (HV) and review

Review and hostile-validation (HV) guidance (operator-directed, 2026-10-09). Applies to every agent, plan, and review loop.

### 7.1 Adversarial review of tracked results (locked 2026-08-12)

1. Validate independently through a hostile reviewer wherever the plan calls for HV and before any done state (section 4.5). Self-check alone is not validation.
2. Every result is timestamped with a sortable local date and time (section 3.1).
3. Every FAIL and UNKNOWN from the review is shown to the operator.
4. Every result includes an accuracy rating and a completeness rating.

Reviewer (resolution of 2026-10-13, verbatim): "HV must not be executed by the same agent family as the requesting agent.  If not specified by operator, ask what agent and model to use for HV in a session." HV uses the reviewer and tooling explicitly authorized for the session. Verify the reviewer's model and effort from its own runtime receipts.

Review time is unbounded (operator, 2026-10-12, verbatim: "Do not bound review time"): no timeout, kill, deadline, or wait limit on any HV reviewer run, and no expected duration in briefs or plans; the implementer only checks the response stream in repeated read-only waits until the run completes, however long the review takes.
